articles.title: Lisandro Martinez red card sums up dysfunction at Man Utd as Brighton post statement win to spark title talk - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: Sky Sports' football writers analyse the Premier League action as Man Utd capitulate at Chelsea, with Estevao a particular highlight for the Blues, while Brighton's rise sparks title talk after they beat Manchester City, Oliver Glasner fumed after Nottingham Forest's latest loss
articles.body:
Lisandro Martinez pointed the finger at technical director Jason Wilcox and the club's hierarchy in his outspoken interview after the Atletico Madrid game . But he only had himself to blame for the events leading to his red card and Chelsea's penalty on Sunday.

There were barely three minutes between the foul on Morgan Rogers that earned him his first yellow card of the afternoon in Manchester United's 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge and the confirmation, from referee Peter Bankes, that he would be receiving a second for needlessly raising an arm to the face of Wesley Fofana in the box.

The defender, starting for the first time since the 1-1 draw against Leeds, was also one of the players at fault for Chelsea's opener, when Rogers glided through United's defence with bewildering ease to set the wheels in motion for United's defeat.

Martinez was not acknowledged by Michael Carrick as he trudged down the tunnel. But the United head coach did not criticise him after the game, albeit while acknowledging the double whammy of having him sent off, and conceding a penalty, was a "big moment" in the game.

It was also a moment to sum up the dysfunction at the club. Nick Wright

Xabi Alonso needed to beat Manchester United to put a stop to the grumblings around the Chelsea fan base. It had been a difficult week and questions were beginning to be asked: and none more so than those about Estevao's limited role in the team.

The Brazilian was handed his first Premier League start of the season at Stamford Bridge and seized his opportunity, leaving the pitch in second-half stoppage-time with the most shots (6), chances created (3) and touches in the opposition box (12).

Still only 19, Alonso is right to be careful with the teenager, but performances like that are only making it harder to keep Estevao out of the Chelsea line-up. Morgan Rogers, who scored a fabulous goal, took most of the plaudits but Estevao was the bigger threat.

His performance deserved a goal and very nearly got one in the second half when he smashed the ball into the roof of the net only for it to be disallowed for offisde by VAR. If he keeps playing like that, sooner or later the youngster will find the back of the net.

Reports had emerged suggesting top clubs in Europe were watching Estevao's situation at Chelsea with increasing interest. Chelsea fans can be reassured by Alonso's explanation about his plan for the teenager. It would be a disaster if the club were to lose him.

Estevao should be considered among Chelsea's untouchables. There has been no better signing of a young talent by the current ownership bar Cole Palmer. That is reflected in Estevao's standing among the Chelsea fans, who refer to him as Steve-O.

This is a player that has the ability to be viewed in the same light as an Eden Hazard or Gianfranco Zola at Stamford Bridge. He is special. Zinny Boswell

Football can be a cruel game, especially for goalkeepers.

Leeds were the better side against Bournemouth in the opening stages. They had started brightly, looked comfortable and were asking questions of the Cherries. Then came the moment that changed everything.

James Trafford's headloss in possession, gifting the ball straight to Justin Kluivert, was an invitation Bournemouth simply could not refuse. Leeds were then chasing a game they had been controlling.

The psychological damage was just as significant as the scoreboard. Leeds never really recovered, their confidence drained by a moment of self-inflicted punishment. Bournemouth had been handed the perfect platform and made sure they took full advantage, winning for the sixth time in a row in all competitions.

Trafford has earned rave reviews since joining Leeds and there is plenty to admire about his potential. But this was a timely reminder that the England international is far from the finished article. Lewis Jones

Brighton's players milked their celebrations with the away end at the Etihad, the first time their supporters had got to indulge in victory at Manchester City. The manner of their recent rise warrants applause - and attention.

Does their latest scalp mean they are in the title race? They are certainly in the conversation. Fabian Hurzeler has built a team who play with complete tactical clarity and has forged a culture everyone seems to buy into. That greatly enhances their chances of doing something special this season, with two statement wins over City and Arsenal as proof things are working.

Enzo Maresca professed to know exactly what Brighton were going to offer up, having hosted them in the Carabao Cup just four days ago, but he could not devise a plan to dent their momentum. City were outbattled in midfield and outrun overall. Brighton deserved their slice of luck to keep a clean sheet.

Hurzeler played down any title talk post-match by emphasising the club's 'game by game' mentality, but if this was a tangible test of Brighton's stomach for the race, they passed with flying colours. Laura Hunter

Nothing changes at Nottingham Forest. Another year of relegation worries, another defeat on Halloween - that's six now straight defeats now on October 31 - and another day when Forest just cannot seem to score.

No wonder Oliver Glasner wants to change things. His explosive post-match press conference effectively said: I will change how we do things and if results don't change, I will be sacked.

Their lack of goalscoring expertise this season was laid bare at Brentford. Forest had 15 shots in west London, all but one were off target. This is despite having Morgan Gibbs-White, one of the top scorers last season, in their team - having also invested in attack-minded players such as Liam Delap and Daniel Munoz over the summer.

And at the back, Forest continue making the same mistakes to concede goals. One long ball from Caoimhin Kelleher put them behind and on the back foot at Brentford - in a similar way they conceded Coventry's winner last month. More and similar mistakes cost them points at Ipswich.

Forest are in another rut and Evangelos Marinakis does not stand for them. Glasner demanded Forest change the "pattern" of the club, but he may not have the time to fully implement those changes. Sam Blitz

It would've been in the spirit of Halloween for the Black Cats to find a way to celebrate the day with a victory. However, their finishing was more of a horror-show for Regis Le Bris to watch.

Enzo Le Fee's penalty was their first goal in the Premier League since they scored three against Manchester City on September 20. However, from open play, their struggles still persist.

They had more than double Coventry's xG this afternoon, albeit inflated from the spot-kick. But, even if they remove that from the equation, they still have slightly more than their opponents (0.80 vs 0.71).

Ultimately, they just weren't anywhere near as clinical when they got in to the areas to punish Coventry. Brian Brobbey looked like a shell of the hat-trick hero at the Etihad. Chemsdine Talbi also wasted a glorious chance.

We have seen it so often where teams qualify for Europe and then struggle the following season. That is what Le Bris is faced with, but at least it is clear where the main problem lies." Callum Bishop

The pressure is continuing to grow on Pierre Sage after the 2-0 loss at Spurs. Every defeat now pushes Steve Parish and Crystal Palace decision-makers closer to making a change.

Since the 5-0 defeat at Brighton, the powers that be have wanted to see defensive improvements in the team and results pick up. Since then they've lost twice in the Premier League, but at least with some improved performances, notably in cup competitions against Besiktas and Fulham.

Palace weren't expected to win at Spurs, especially after going down to 10 men, but they're now in the bottom three with Liverpool visiting Selhurst Park next Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

A vulnerability from set-pieces has been a theme under Sage, which again will be a worry for the hierarchy.

For the second game running, Palace's away support chanted Sage's name; there's an understanding from them he's been dealt a tough hand after losing Maxence Lacroix and Daniel Munoz in the summer. And the players at Spurs certainly didn't show a lack of effort; in fact, it was the opposite, they put in a shift.

But this is a results business, as Sage has admitted himself, and Parish hasn't been afraid to make ruthless decisions: think back to Patrick Vieira.

It feels right that Sage should get fixtures against Coventry and Hull to prove himself, but football isn't always so kind. The performances against Fulham in the Carabao Cup and Tottenham tonight have at least shown fight and resilience.

It's going to be another interesting few days waiting to see if Parish and co stick or twist. Chris Reidy

There was plenty to admire about Hull's second-half response, but there is a nagging feeling they are in danger of letting some of that early-season goodwill slip away.

They were a different side after the break. More aggressive, more purposeful and with far greater conviction.

Tim Iroegbunam and Oli McBurnie turned the game on its head, while the latter's work rate and influence gave the hosts something to build around.

For a spell, they looked capable of securing a result that would have meant plenty.

But the concern is becoming harder to ignore. Hull have now gone seven league games without a win after taking maximum points from their first two.

Their spirited performances and promising start have bought them patience, but that will not last forever.

They cannot keep relying on character to paper over slow starts and missed opportunities.

There are positives here, certainly, but Sergej Jakirovic needs to turn them into wins before frustration starts to take hold. William Bitibiri

There was something rather telling about the reaction of the Fulham players to their travelling supporters at full-time. This was not a team celebrating a point like they had got away with something. It was a team that knew they had given their fans plenty to shout about.

Fulham were excellent for large parts of their 1-1 draw at Aston Villa. They took the game to Unai Emery's side, dictated the tempo for long spells and created enough opportunities to leave Villa Park feeling they should have taken more.

The underlying numbers reinforce the eye test. Fulham generated 2.2 expected goals, the fifth-highest total recorded by any visiting team at Villa Park since the start of the 2023/24 season. They also registered 40 touches inside the Villa penalty area. That is serious territorial dominance against a side who rarely allow opponents to dictate terms on home soil.

This feels like a Fulham team beginning to find its feet. There is more purpose to their attacking play, more conviction in possession and a growing belief that they can compete with the division's better sides. Lewis Jones

articles.title: Luis García Plaza, sobre Bordalás: "Es el mejor entrenador en la historia del Getafe"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Sevilla también destacó que "los que han elevado el nivel del equipo realmente son los que ya estaban"
articles.summary: El técnico del Sevilla también destacó que "los que han elevado el nivel del equipo realmente son los que ya estaban"
articles.body: Este sábado, Luis García Plaza atendió a los medios en la previa de la undécima jornada de LaLiga EA Sports, en la que el Sevilla visitará mañana al Getafe en el Coliseum (14:00 horas). "Primero, dar mi pésame a todas las familias que han sufrido el accidente y también mandar un mensaje de esperanza a todas las familias que tienen algún desaparecido o herido. Como cualquier persona, tenemos que seguir con nuestro trabajo y honrar nuestra profesión con la memoria de lo que nos ha pasado", comenzó el preparador sevillista. Getafe. "Para mí es un partido muy difícil. El Getafe tiene dos caras completamente diferentes. Es el peor equipo de la categoría fuera de casa. Sin embargo, en casa está invicto, compitiendo muy bien, saben a lo que juegan y con delanteros muy potentes. Quitando a los de arriba, tiene de las mejores delanteras de la Liga con ese juego directo y tenemos que dar lo mejor de nosotros". Base de la temporada anterior. "Estamos súper contentos con todos los chicos que han venido nuevos, que nos están aportando esa frescura y venían sin esa carga psicológica. El otro día jugaron siete de inicio de la temporada pasada. Entonces, los que para mí han elevado el nivel del equipo realmente son los que ya estaban: Castrín, Kike Salas, Odyssea, Gaby, Luci, Isaac, Chidi… encantado con los fichajes, pero lo que le ha dado ese salto de calidad al equipo, quitando a Fofana, son ellos. El año pasado oí críticas muy duras hacia ellos, y ahora están jugando a un nivel excepcional. Hay que darle valor". Ambiente de crispación. "Tengo un cariño muy grande al Getafe. Estuve tres años allí. Creo que el trabajo de Pepe es innegable. Es el mejor entrenador de la historia del Getafe. Yo soy el segundo con más partidos allí, pero desde luego ni llego a la altura. No tengo ni idea de lo que va a pasar, tengo una gran relación con Ángel, con el presi. Es un tío que hay que valorarle todo lo que ha hecho en el Getafe y lo que ha construido. En casa han sido merecedores de esos resultados, y fuera los he visto flojos. Estoy seguro de que van a ir a tope". Estilo Bordalás. "Los mejores Getafe de Pepe son gente que de defensiva tiene poca. Otra cosa es que juegue más directo, más vertical, en campo contrario, te presiona arriba... Tal vez sea un estilo físico. Enes y Satriano son ganadores de duelos. Hay que tener claro que es el estilo que hay y te obliga a estar muy atrás metido". Centrales. "Están muy bien los dos. Yo creo que también se conocen. Se compenetran. Kike está en un nivel muy alto. Es mi sensación. Y Sangante yo creo que está preparado para jugar porque lo veo entrenar y veo su actitud trabajadora". Tres partidos en seis días. "La gente que jugó más tiempo no ha entrenado prácticamente. Los he visto hacer el calentamiento y los hemos sacado. Los que jugaron 60 minutos pueden jugar, participar, pero la gente que jugó 90 es difícil que juegue mañana de titular. Hemos subido a diez chicos de las categorías inferiores que quiero agradecerles su predisposición para trabajar. Para eso están las plantillas".

articles.title: The exact points that separated Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe  in Ballon d'Or race revealed as official voting figures emerge
articles.summary: Harry Kane clinches the 2026 Ballon d'Or in a tight race against Kylian Mbappe, with just 28 points separating the two soccer stars. Discover the voting breakdown and historical context of this remarkable contest.
articles.body: Harry Kane's first Ballon d'Or came after a much tighter contest than the final announcement might have suggested. Kylian Mbappe finished just 28 points behind the Bayern Munich striker, with the official voting figures now revealing how the 100-member jury divided its support between the two leading contenders.Kane edges Mbappe after a closely fought voteKane finished with 1,055 points from the 100 journalists who voted for the men's Ballon d'Or, just 28 ahead of Kylian Mbappe, who received 1,027. The narrow gap shows just how close the race was between the two stars.Kane was named the winner on 40 of the 100 voting ballots, while Mbappe received the top spot on 23. Those votes helped the England captain secure the award, although Mbappe remained firmly in contention until the final results were counted.Kane lifted the trophy at the London Palladium on Monday evening, becoming the first Englishman to win the men's Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001. He earned the honour after scoring 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England during the 2025-26 season, helping Bayern win a domestic Treble and captaining England to third place at the World Cup.For Mbappe, it was another near miss in his first attempt to win the award. Kane's 28-point lead was also smaller than the 41-point gap between Rodri and Vinicius Junior in 2024, making this one of the closest Ballon d'Or races in recent years.Where Kane's victory ranks among the closest Ballon d'Or decisionsAlthough Kane and Mbappe were separated by only 28 points, their contest was not the closest in the award's history. The figures released by L'Equipe place it among the more closely contested recent editions, but several previous winners have prevailed by even smaller margins.Lionel Messi defeated Virgil van Dijk by seven points in 2019, making it the narrowest margin of recent voting contests. The result followed a season in which Van Dijk had helped Liverpool win the Champions League, while Messi collected his sixth Ballon d'Or.The historical margins become even tighter when earlier editions are considered. Matthias Sammer beat Brazilian forward Ronaldo by a single point in 1996, while Sir Bobby Charlton also finished one point ahead of Eusebio in 1966. Only 22 people voted in that 1966 edition, a considerably smaller electorate than the international panel used today.The comparison is useful because the Ballon d'Or's voting structure has changed considerably over the decades. Kane's 28-point victory came from a system in which 100 journalists each selected 10 players, giving every ballot considerably more scope to influence the final standings than the smaller electorate of earlier editions.How the 2026 Ballon d'Or voting system workedThe official breakdown covers the top 10 in both the men's and women's awards. The men's panel consisted of 100 journalists, while 50 journalists voted for the Ballon d'Or Feminin, making 150 voters across the two categories.Under the system introduced in 2022, the men's award is voted on by journalists representing the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings, while the women's award uses representatives from the top 50. Only one journalist from each eligible country is entitled to submit a ballot.Each voter selects 10 players from the respective list of 30 nominees. The players are then awarded points according to their position on each ballot: 15 for first place, 12 for second, 10 for third, followed by eight, seven, five, four, three, two and one point.That structure means the maximum possible score is 1,500 points for the men's award and 750 for the women's. Kane's 1,055 points represented more than two-thirds of the maximum available, while Mbappe's 1,027 left him only 28 behind.The awards considered performances during the 2025-26 season. That distinction also applied to players whose circumstances changed after the campaign: Rodri, who now plays for Barcelona, was assessed on his performances for Manchester City and his World Cup success with Spain.The men's top 10 showed a substantial gap between the leading pair and the rest of the field. Barcelona's Lamine Yamal finished third with 881 points, 146 behind Mbappe and 174 short of Kane. Rodri was fourth with 726, followed by Lionel Messi on 612.The men's Ballon d'Or 2026: Official top 10PositionPlayerClub and countryPoints1Harry KaneBayern Munich and England1,0552Kylian MbappeReal Madrid and France1,0273Lamine YamalBarcelona and Spain8814RodriManchester City and Spain7265Lionel MessiInter Miami and Argentina6126Khvicha KvaratskheliaParis Saint-Germain and Georgia5417Ousmane DembeleParis Saint-Germain and France4188Erling HaalandManchester City and Norway3789Michael OliseBayern Munich and France29610Fabian RuizParis Saint-Germain and Spain201Putellas wins the women's award, but the lower places are exceptionally tightThe women's Ballon d'Or produced a more comfortable victory at the top, although the voting figures also revealed several close contests further down the standings. Alexia Putellas won the award for a third time, equalling the record held by her Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati.Putellas, who now plays for London City Lionesses after representing Barcelona during the 2025-26 season, received 618 points. Her former Barcelona team-mate Ewa Pajor finished second with 532, leaving an 86-point gap between them. Putellas' total was also more than four-fifths of the maximum 750 points available in the women's vote.The battle for third place was particularly close. Manchester City forward Bunny Shaw collected 334 points, just two more than Lyon's Melchie Dumornay, who finished on 332.There was also little to separate the players further down the rankings. Patri Guijarro finished fifth with 221 points, while Caroline Graham Hansen and Pernille Harder both collected 220. As the two players were tied on points, their final positions were decided by the number of first-place votes, with Graham Hansen placed sixth and Harder seventh.Claudia Pina and Arsenal's Alessia Russo also finished level on 155 points. articles.title: Jonathan Viera anuncia que cuelga las botas y su futuro está en los banquillos
articles.standfirst: El grancanario comienza con sus cursos para ser entrenador
articles.summary: Comienza su preparación para ser entrenador
articles.body: Jonathan Viera no bailará más sobre el césped. El futbolista grancanario, de 37 años, pone punto final a una trayectoria profesional marcada por su talento, su calidad técnica y, especialmente, su estrecho vínculo con la UD Las Palmas, el club de su vida. Formado en la cantera amarilla, debutó con el primer equipo en 2010 y, tras cinco etapas en la entidad, se marcha dejando unos números de 295 partidos oficiales y 76 goles. Su legado está ligado a los dos ascensos a Primera división conseguidos en las temporadas 2014-15 y 2022-23, además de haberse convertido en uno de los grandes referentes del fútbol canario de las últimas décadas. Fuera de Gran Canaria, defendió las camisetas del Valencia, el Rayo Vallecano y el Almería, además del Standard de Lieja belga, el Beijing Guoan chino, el Johor malasio, el Khor Fakkan de Emiratos y el Ratchaburi tailandés, donde disputó su última experiencia profesional. Su trayectoria también tuvo reconocimiento internacional con el debut en la selección española absoluta el 6 de octubre de 2017, en un encuentro frente a Albania correspondiente a la fase de clasificación para el Mundial de Rusia 2018. El adiós a los terrenos de juego no significa, sin embargo, una despedida definitiva del fútbol. Viera ya ha manifestado su intención de iniciar una nueva etapa en los banquillos y convertirse en entrenador a medio plazo. Para ello, tiene previsto obtener las titulaciones correspondientes antes de dar el salto a la dirección técnica. El propio futbolista ha reconocido que uno de sus grandes sueños sería regresar algún día a la UD Las Palmas, esta vez desde el banquillo. Una posibilidad que contempla con ilusión. El Mago de La Feria cierra así su etapa como futbolista, pero mantiene abierta la puerta a seguir vinculado al club que marcó su carrera.

articles.title: Todo el campo es del Atlético
articles.standfirst: Una jugada que empieza en Oblak y acaba en Giuliano sirve como perfecto resumen del gran partido del equipo rojiblanco, que antes ya se manejaba con ventaja tras otro gol de Grimaldo
articles.summary: Una jugada que empieza en Oblak y acaba en Giuliano sirve como perfecto resumen del gran partido del equipo rojiblanco, que antes ya se manejaba con ventaja tras otro gol de Grimaldo
articles.body: Pasó la pelota por Oblak, para gloria de este Atlético que procura siempre y consigue casi siempre sacar la pelota limpia. Después de que la tocara el de las manoplas discurrió aún por los dominios de Pubill y Llorente, pero fue Barrios el que aclaró toda la acción con una maniobra espléndida cerca de la banda para habilitar la autopista que Baena apuró hasta encontrar a Giuliano. A su pierna izquierda, concretamente, dándose la paradoja de que, con el césped poniendo también de su parte, la definición fue prácticamente lo peor de una grandísima jugada. Tanto dio, porque definición fue al fin y al cabo. Era el segundo visitante y coronaba un tramo espléndido, posterior al refrigerio, en el que ya se había invalidado una diana a Hancko por posición antirreglamentaria, en el que Kang-in había topado con el larguero y en el que el propio Guliano había flirteado con la portería de Ryan. Todo desde un dominio colectivo que devolvió las certezas rojiblancas después de dos partidos de dudas. Si la desventaja mínima anterior alimentaba la sospecha de que el Levante se viniera arriba en esa segunda parte, ya se encargó el Atlético de dinamitar cualquier puente hacia tal posibilidad. Golpe de autoridad para ponerse pero que muy arriba. La puesta en escena granota había resultado notable mucho antes, diez minutos de determinación en los que el Atlético estuvo a verlas venir y en los que Oblak salvó los muebles visitantes volando para evitar la que había tenido a Requena en el origen y en la resolución. Aquello fue espejismo, en todo caso, porque, esta vez sí, el equipo de Simeone atendió al origen de sus males y se fue haciendo fuerte a partir de la pelota, para diseñar un segundo tramo de partido interesante y que además resultó mucho más largo que el anterior, de hecho llegó prácticamente hasta el descanso. Ese cambio de tendencia vino a coincidir con el primer susto que se llevó la tropa granota, Hjulmand pinchando y poniendo en la jaula un servicio de Baena... aunque también en fuera de juego, éste delatado después por la tecnología. Precisamente el danés estaba en la base de la mejoría rojiblanca, pendiente siempre de hacerse con la pelota para que luego la movieran los de la misma camiseta. Kang-in y Llorente probaron suerte desde fuera del área, disparo desviado en el caso del primero, mano espléndida de Ryan para el segundo, para demostrar definitivamente que el Atlético se había hecho con el timón. Sorprendía que el Levante esperara atrás, permitiendo conducciones, sobre todo después de aquel arranque intenso, el caso es que, llegados a ese punto, fue a equivocarse uno de los futbolistas más fiables de la temporada local. Porque el servicio de Baena no hubiera llegado a Grimaldo en condiciones normales, pero Olasagasti pifió al despejar permitiendo el mano a mano de un lateral que gozó de tiempo para levantar la cabeza y preparar ese cañón que tiene por zurda. A 116 kilómetros por hora la vio pasar Ryan. Desequilibrado el marcador por fin, el Atlético mantuvo la compostura hasta que De Burgos abrió el paréntesis del entreacto. Luego pasó lo que pasó, que aquello fue monólogo hasta que se movieron los banquillos, de hecho no parece casualidad que Etta Eyong lamentara la gran ocasión del Levante justo después de que Simeone hiciera las primeras sustituciones. Tampoco se trata de que Sorloth y Jonathan David tuvieran incidencia directa en la acción, pero parecía evidente que, tal y como estaba manejándose el Atlético, cualquier cambio sería a peor. Luis Castro, de perdidos al río, respondió además con uno cuádruple. Aun aparecerían otros protagonistas, entre ellos Marc Santos con sus insultantes 15 años, pero aquello ya no daba para más. Así que otra portería a cero para Oblak. Para el del segundo gol de un magnífico Atlético, sí.

articles.title: Why Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, refuses to drink milk: Inside the diet and discipline behind his longevity, according to former chef
articles.summary: Discover Cristiano Ronaldo's strict dietary choices that contribute to his remarkable longevity in football, including his aversion to milk and emphasis on nutritious meals.
articles.body: At 41, Cristiano Ronaldo is still chasing a milestone that once seemed beyond the reach of any footballer, with his career tally approaching 1,000 goals after another prolific season for Al-Nassr. His longevity has been built on an unusually disciplined approach to training, recovery and nutrition, although one of the strictest rules in his diet concerns a food that many athletes regard as an everyday source of protein and calcium. According to his former private chef, Giorgio Barone, Ronaldo does not drink milk at all.Why Ronaldo refuses to drink milkMilk is commonly included in athletes’ diets because of its protein, calcium and other nutrients, with many players using it as part of their recovery routine. Ronaldo, however, has avoided dairy as part of his long-standing nutritional approach, a decision his former private chef says reflects more than a preference about taste or performance.Giorgio Barone, who previously worked as Ronaldo’s private chef, explained that milk was completely excluded from the forward’s diet because of his views on humans consuming the milk of other animals.“No milk,” Barone told Covers.com, before explaining his reasoning.“Humans are the only animals that drink the milk of other animals. No other animal drinks milk after three months. Calves don’t drink milk after the age of three months. Animals don’t drink the milk of other animals.“It does not exist in nature. Only human beings continue to drink milk up to 30, 40, 50, and 60 years, and in my view it is wrong. We breastfeed from our mothers, like dogs, wolves, cows and donkeys. It is normal.“After infancy it is not normal. It is against nature.”Barone's explanation is his own view of nutrition, rather than an established medical consensus, but it illustrates how deliberately Ronaldo has approached the food he consumes throughout his career. Dairy is not the only category he avoids, with the Portuguese forward also known for steering clear of refined sugar, processed foods and alcohol.What Ronaldo eats throughout the dayBarone described Ronaldo's diet as balanced rather than built around a single food group, with the emphasis placed on fresh ingredients, lean protein and vegetables. The former chef said the forward eats a little of everything, provided it meets the standards of his nutritional routine.“Cristiano Ronaldo’s diet is balanced,” he said. “He eats a little bit of everything, but it’s always healthy.”Breakfast typically includes avocado, coffee and eggs, with no added sugar. Lunch can consist of chicken or fish accompanied by vegetables, while dinner is generally lighter, with fish or meat served alongside vegetables.“Starting with breakfast, he would have an avocado with coffee, eggs and no sugar. Absolutely no sugar. Lunch could be chicken, fish and always vegetables. If he needs carbohydrates, he gets them through vegetables, so he doesn’t need anything made with flour.“Nothing like pasta, bread and other types of food. In the evening, he eats light foods, usually fish or meat in the form of fillet. It’s always accompanied by vegetables.”The broader nutritional approach described in the additional account of Ronaldo's routine includes as many as six high-protein meals a day, spaced three to four hours apart. Chicken, cod, sea bass, fresh vegetables and avocado feature prominently, while quinoa and other whole grains provide carbohydrate sources alongside the vegetables mentioned by Barone. The emphasis remains on whole foods and consistent meals rather than relying on processed products or sugary snacks.That routine is designed to support the physical demands of a player who continues to compete at the highest level well into his forties. Ronaldo's body fat has been reported at below 10 per cent, with some accounts putting it at around seven per cent, although the exact figure can vary with the timing and method of measurement.The training and recovery behind his longevityRonaldo's approach extends well beyond what he eats. His training combines high-intensity sprinting, plyometric exercises and explosive strength work with Pilates and other forms of conditioning, while recovery has remained an important part of his daily routine.His recovery methods include sauna sessions, ice baths and cryotherapy, with his partner Georgina Rodriguez also known to join him for some of those activities.Sleep is another area in which Ronaldo has reportedly adopted an unconventional approach. Rather than relying solely on one long overnight period, he utilizes polyphasic sleep to optimize his recovery. His routine consists of five 90-minute naps spaced throughout the day, a strategy meticulously designed to maintain high metabolic energy levels and maximize cellular repair between intense training sessions.The combination of nutrition, training and recovery has helped Ronaldo remain physically competitive across a career spanning more than two decades. His longevity has also made him unusually conscious of the small decisions that can affect his preparation, from the food he eats to the time he gives his body to recover between matches.One of the most visible examples of his attitude towards nutrition came during the 2021 European Championship. At a press conference, Ronaldo moved bottles of Coca-Cola away from the table and encouraged viewers to “drink water”. The gesture attracted enormous attention and was followed by a reported fall in Coca-Cola's market value.Why Ronaldo's former chef agrees with Haaland about organ meatBarone also discussed the differences between Ronaldo's nutritional choices and those of Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, who has spoken about including raw milk in his diet. The two approaches differ on dairy, but Barone agreed with Haaland's preference for organ meats, which he considers particularly nutritious.“I agree with [Erling Haaland’s diet of] eating the organs. The liver, heart and brain are all healthy foods. They are superfoods. Cristiano liked liver too. I love it. It’s very rich in iron, and it’s important in the diet, so for the organs, I approve, but not for the milk.”Ronaldo's customized routine has continued to attract global attention because of what he manages to sustain on the pitch. The 41-year-old forward has elevated his historic, all-time record tally to 985 official career goals following a masterful performance for Al-Nassr. His latest Saudi Pro League appearance against Al-Kholood featured a dazzling 15-minute hat-trick that secured a thrilling 5-3 victory. This incredible treble marked the 67th senior career hat-trick for the Portuguese icon, extending his unparalleled scoring record even further ahead of long-time rival Lionel Messi.The performance came shortly after Ronaldo was named the winner of the inaugural B.O.A.T. award, or Ballon d'Or of All Time, following a global fan poll that selected his 2008 season with Manchester United as the greatest peak campaign. With the updated career total placing him 15 goals short of 1,000, the milestone is now a realistic target as he continues to lead Al-Nassr and Portugal.His pursuit of that record has brought renewed attention to the discipline behind his career, including the strict nutritional choices described by Barone. For Ronaldo, avoiding milk is one part of a much larger routine built around consistency, preparation and the demands of remaining an elite footballer at 41.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luís Castro: "Las emociones te hacen mirar el resultado de una manera diferente"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador portugués entiende que su equipo mereció mejor suerte
articles.summary: El entrenador portugués entiende que su equipo mereció mejor suerte
articles.body: El entrenador portugués ha ensalzado el trabajo mental de los suyos hasta el último momento del choque, a pesar del resultado. "Ellos tienen buen equipo y tienen muy buena calidad, pero tu terminas el partido con más remates y con más goles esperados. Has tenido los mejores remates. En la segunda parte entras mejor que ellos. Ha sido un partido en el que primer error, te hacen daño. Yo no me quiero quedar con una impresión del resultado solo. Las emociones te hacen mirar el resultado de una manera diferente. Yo he visto a equipos que se quedan defendiendo todo el partido y terminan empatando o ganando. Hoy has peleado y has tenido las mejores oportunidades, pero ellos, cuando las ha tenido, la han metido dentro. Hay días así, pero me quiero quedar con lo que el equipo ha hecho. Si Olsas no hace mal control y Requena la mete dentro, te quedas con sensación que has hecho un partido. Para mí, ellos están mejor colectivamente que el año pasado y han tenido la capacidad de no vender a ninguno" "Todos los partidos te aportan cosas para mejorar. No hicimos mal partido, pero siempre hay cosas para mejorar. Siempre hay cosas buenas para mejorar. Hay que seguir adelante con el mismo carácter de siempre, siendo un equipo humilde y pelear por todos los partidos. No hay que perder la identidad" "Manu tiene una pequeña lesión y ha jugado todos los partidos. Teníamos tres decisiones y pensamos que, por las características del choque, nos podía aportar y como habéis visto, entramos algunas veces por la derecha, y sabíamos que Toljan en el tramo final, como es un jugador con más experiencia, y podría afrontar mejor los momentos. Nacho es bueno a nivel defensivo y pensamos que esa era la decisión correcta" "Etta ha estado bien. Ha tenido situaciones y ha atacado en situaciones como queremos. Vendrás goles y ha ayudado al equipo. Ha hecho mucho esfuerzo a nivel colectivos. Está mejorando cada día que pasa y pienso que estará cerca como nos gusta" "Ha estado normal como siempre. Muy buenas decisiones. Con un carácter muy fuerte y no es fácil entrar en un partido como esté. Ha mostrado una personalidad, como siempre. Está con nivel para jugar, tanto a nivel con balón bajo o como el centro a Brugué. No es una novedad par a nosotros y es normal para las personas que no lo conocen una novedad" "No he visto. Tengo que hablar con el cuerpo técnico. Seguro que sería algo que necesitaría. A veces tiene algunos dolores, como es normal, pero juega porque está al 100% para competir. No te puedo decir que es esto porque te mentiría" "He hablado con el árbitro y ya está todo hablado" "Marc tiene 15 años y está creciendo. Es un jugador que ha pasado de jugar abajo, sin pasar por el equipo B. Está creciendo mucho. Ha entrado en los partidos y hoy ha entrado porque necesitábamos calidad de atacar y cuando lo metes, es porque crees que aportará. Es muy inteligente y yo tengo alguna experiencia con jugadores jóvenes y sé que las etapas se deben hacer cuando se deben hacer. Yo no quiero que se quede toda la vida sin oportunidades. Hoy ha entrado muy bien porque yo sabía que estaba a nivel que podría aportar. Es un jugador de la primera plantilla, lo he visto mil veces, y lo sé seguro. Nos da garantías que puede jugar en más de una posición. Si juega titular o no, dependerá no solo de él, si no de los adversarios de mis decisiones. Con su edad, tanto en pretemporada como en partidos oficiales, ha estado a un buen nivel. Nos da información que, hará errores como Ryan, Mandi o Toljan, pero es uno de los jugadores que tiene un buen camino" "No pienso así porque has terminado el partido con el Atlético defendiendo con todo y si, nos hubiera hecho daño mentalmente, no hubiéramos terminando así. Hemos estado hasta el último minuto para ganar. Pienso que no ha afectado para nada al equipo y ha continuidad con la misma dinámica hasta el final"

articles.title: Kilmarnock 2-2 St Johnstone: St Johnstone fight back from Toby Steward's early dismissal to take point at Kilmarnock
articles.summary: Report as St Johnstone fight back from Toby Steward's early dismissal to take a point away at Kilmarnock in an entertaining Scottish Premiership affair
articles.body:
Simo Valakari's side were at a disadvantage from the 13th minute following the dismissal of goalkeeper Toby Steward for handling outside of his area.

Yet despite going behind immediately after the red card to Cathal McCarthy's first goal, Saints were never out of the game.

They levelled through Danny Schmidt after 40 minutes, only for Djenairo Daniels to restore the home lead before half-time.

However, a breakaway goal from Joel Cotterill after 65 minutes was enough to claim an unlikely point.

The game was turned on its head after just 10 minutes when Steward was sent off following a costly error. The on-loan Portsmouth goalkeeper came rushing out of his penalty area to deal with a long ball, with Joe Hugill bearing down on goal.

Steward appeared to have time to take a step back before gathering the ball, but VAR advised referee Matthew MacDermid to review the incident for a denial of a goalscoring opportunity. The goalkeeper was shown a red card.

Sinclair, brought on in place of Taylor Steven, was immediately thrown into the action and had to pick the ball out of his net with his first touch.

From the resulting set-piece, Kilmarnock worked the ball for Greg Kiltie to deliver an inswinging cross, which McCarthy met six yards out with a header to score the first goal of his loan spell from Hull City.

Daniels thought he had doubled the lead after 31 minutes from a tight angle before an offside flag foiled him.

Kilmarnock's defensive problems first came back to bite them, even with the personnel advantage, five minutes before half-time.

Josh Fowler was denied by an excellent fingertip stop by German keeper Nico Mantl but, from the corner, Enes Alic's delivery was headed into the far corner by an unmarked Schmidt.

Kilmarnock did not dwell on their misfortune and hit straight back. Hugill scampered up the left flank and his cutback was buried by a brilliant backheel flick from Daniels.

Aaron Tshibola missed a golden opportunity to put Saints to bed after 63 minutes. Hugill's brilliant backheel sent the DR Congo international through on goal, but his weak effort was straight at Sinclair.

Saints stunned Killie just two minutes later to level the scores once more.

The equaliser came after Kilmarnock's corner broke down, allowing Alic to pick out Cotterill with an excellent pass. The Welshman burst beyond two defenders before drilling a low finish into the net to make it 2-2.

Nicky Clescenco came within inches of restoring Killie's lead after Tyreece John-Jules robbed Diabate of possession.

Sinclair then kept Saints in the game, first pushing away George Stanger's effort before producing a superb reflex save to deny John-Jules from close range as Kilmarnock continued to search for a winner.

"Toby has held his hands up and said: 'I am sorry, boys, for what I did.'

"But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor (Steven), who I needed to take out straight away.

"We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other's backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility.

"Early red card, with Toby that's my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a 'sweeper keeper' for those long balls.

"In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It's a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen."

"The quality evaded us. We're in a 2-1 lead and we concede from our set-piece - that's not good enough against 10 men.

"It's really painful because we do a lot of work on set-pieces. It feels like a defeat. Even though we've taken a point, it's like we've thrown away two.

"I completely understand why the fans are angry because I am too. We had lots of control in the game but that Achilles heel of chucking up soft goals is something that's plaguing us right now."

articles.title: De Frutos devuelve la primavera a Vallecas
articles.standfirst: Goleada del Rayo en la primera fiesta de la temporada en casa
articles.summary: Goleada del Rayo en la primera fiesta de la temporada en casa
articles.body: Primavera en otoño. ¿Y qué? En Vallecas las estaciones dependen de los estados de ánimo, no de la inclinación del eje de la Tierra. Después del exilio en Butarque, de la protesta ante el Athletic y de la tristísima tarde sin fondo que acabó en goleada del Elche, por fin el barrio explotó de alegría. En una semana en la que lo único bueno que nos dejó el fútbol fue la ayuda de los aficionados rayistas a las víctimas del accidente de trenes de Urda, el balón se lo supo recompensar. El partido se calentó en menos de un minuto, lo que tardó el Celta en sacar su primer córner. El Rayo aceptó el reto y se tiró también con todo al área rival, pero con más ganas y mejor juego. Radu le hizo un paradón a Camello en el minuto 15 y los de Giráldez empezaron a pasar mucho tiempo en su propio campo. Un rato después Rueda se tiró con tanto entusiasmo a defender un pase que olía a gol que obligó a hacer una buena parada a su portero, que le miró con ojos traviesos con reproche. No tardó mucho más en caer el primero. Álvaro encontró a Camello y el 10 metió un gran pase de caño para la carrera de De Frutos, que definió de primeras, con la zurda, pegadita al palo e imposible para Radu. Era el primer gol de la temporada en Vallecas, que lo celebró desbordándose como si acabara de quitar un tapón de la garganta. El descanso le sirvió al Rayo para recargar ánimo y al Celta para dedicarse al reconcome, al "qué mal estamos", al "pero qué nos pasa". Y eso se notó nada más empezar el segundo tiempo. De Frutos hizo un jugadón rompiendo líneas, pero su disparo no fue del todo contundente y acabó en las manos de Radu. En el 55' no pasó lo mismo. Ratiu, funambulista en zonas inesperadas, se tiró un sombrero de espaldas ante dos rivales en la frontal y asistió tras un truco digno de Zidane para De Frutos, que se acordó de la acción anterior y soltó un zapatazo que se coló casi por la escuadra de la portería del Celta. El Celta se quedó pasmado y sin reacción, mientras Vallecas celebraba por fin. Y quedaba la guinda. Unai López cogió un balón lejísimos de la portería, se fue acercando a la frontal y, con el interior y buscando el palo con suavidad, batió a Radu con un golazo. El Celta no tiró ni a puerta. Los de Giráldez parecen a veces este año de un celeste pálido, lejos del brillo de un juego que maravillaba en LaLiga. Y lo peor de estar en ese laberinto es que parece que no saben ni cómo se han metido ahí ni mucho menos cómo encontrar la salida. En Vallecas, brotes verdes. Todavía no florece la alegría, pero al menos asoma. A ver si la siguen regando.

articles.title: Tablas en una tarde de Halloween
articles.standfirst: Al partido disputado en Ipurua no le faltó de nada
articles.summary: Al partido disputado en Ipurua no le faltó de nada
articles.body: Eibar y Almería firmaron las tablas en un encuentro que tuvo de todo, desde dominios alternos, hasta accidentes en la grada y en el césped. Por suerte, todo quedó en una anécdota y lo que terminó prevaleciendo fue un encuentro emocionante hasta el final entre dos de los mejores equipos de la competición hasta la fecha. Quim Junyent adelantó a los visitantes y Pejiño se inventó una obra de arte para cerrar la puerta a la derrota. El Almería impuso su plan de entrada. García Pimienta no renunció al balón. El equipo indálico atraía en la salida de balón para hacer correr a un Eibar impreciso cuando tenía que robar en campo contrario. Los armeros tomaban riesgos en la presión, pero no fueron capaces de recuperar cerca de la portería rival ni tampoco tras pérdida. El contexto parecía propicio para los rojiblancos con Arribas y Junyent al mando de las operaciones. Por quinto partido consecutivo, el Eibar empezó por detrás en el marcador. Una gran jugada colectiva, con un pase por arriba de De La Fuente sobre Arribas para servir en bandeja el gol a Junyent. 0-1. El partido entonces se detuvo, porque un aficionado visitante cayó de forma peligrosa al césped en plena celebración, y el colegiado mandó a los jugadores a los vestuarios. Aranbarri aprovechó la pausa para hacer algunos ajustes y por suerte, todo quedó en un susto. El tanto del catalán obligó al Eibar a llevar la iniciativa. Sin mucho éxito. El Almería es un equipo que también sabe convivir en bloque bajo y apenas dio opciones a los locales en una primera mitad sin demasiadas ocasiones. El balón era armero, pero la sensación es que el Almería estaba más cómodo sobre el campo y era capaz de controlar el partido con y sin balón. El inicio de la segunda mitad no cambió nada. El Eibar con falta de fluidez y el Almería gestionando sin demasiado estrés sus momentos de repliegue. Sin embargo, en Ipurua siempre hay un tramo en el que los locales, hasta en sus días grises, tienen su momento. Y el Almería tampoco pudo huir de ello. Iván Gil avisó con un remate desde la frontal, Adu metió el miedo en el cuerpo al rival con un remate al palo y Pejiño, en los minutos finales, se sacó un latigazo desde fuera del área a la escuadra para el delirio de los eibarreses. Aún quedaba tiempo para más. El Eibar soñó con la victoria, pero pudo perder el punto rescatado en la última jugada, en un disparo de Gui Guedes que impactó en el larguero. Un empate que deja un mejor regusto en los armeros, que acumulan dos jornadas seguidas en Ipurua rescatando dos empates sobre la bocina ante dos candidatos al ascenso. El Almería continúa puntuando y ya van nueve jornadas seguidas sin caer.

articles.title: Giráldez: “Debemos reflexionar, no vale el nivel que hemos dado hoy”
articles.standfirst: No le gustó nada su equipo defensivamente
articles.summary: No le gustó nada su equipo defensivamente
articles.body: Decepcionado con el rendimiento de su equipo, fundamentalmente en el aspecto defensivo, y autocrítico se mostró Claudio Giráldez, tras la derrota en Vallecas. Derrota justa: “Hemos defendido mal y cuando lo haces te vas con tres y han podido ser cuatro porque ha tenido Radu una parada muy buena. Hemos perdido mucha situación de juego directo, de duelo, y hemos permitido al Rayo correr, que es lo que mejor hace, por lo que defensivamente hemos estado muy mal. Hemos tenido momentos de juego buenos, llegadas para generar más. Nos vamos con una sensación muy mala porque hay que aprovechar las ventajas que te da el juego y generar mucho más peligro”. Derrota para reflexionar: “Hemos tenido una derrota dura y debemos reflexionar sobre ello y no vale el nivel que hemos dado hoy. El primer responsable, evidentemente, soy yo. Cuando no vas con la intensidad que requiere un partido profesional, ya no hablo de Primera división, te acaban generando peligro”. Imagen: “No es la que queremos. Hubo momentos en el partido que no aprovechamos y nos vamos con una sensación de impotencia. Hemos hecho un mal partido y te lo penaliza un equipo que ha estado inspirado y ha ganado con merecimiento”. Levantar el ánimo: “Es el primer partido que perdemos fuera de casa en Liga en cinco jornadas, que son números positivos y llevábamos siete jornadas sin perder en Liga”.

articles.title: Oliver Glasner: Nottingham Forest head coach reveals anger, desire to change growing pattern at club amid poor start to season
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest were beaten 2-0 by Brentford and remain in the relegation zone; Oliver Glasner's side are the lowest scorers in the Premier League this season and it has prompted an angry response from the Forest head coach; Glasner is Forest's fifth head coach since August 2025
articles.body:
Forest fans booed off their team after a 2-0 loss at Brentford left them in the relegation zone for another week. They are also the Premier League's lowest scorers this season with six goals from nine games.

With Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis known as a ruthless decision-maker, that supporter anger was shared by Glasner at full-time and in an explosive press conference, the Forest head coach said:

he has made too many compromises with this Forest team since the start of the season;

he takes responsibility for the poor form this season, but the club are in the "same s*** situation" each year;

Forest needs to change from top to bottom after a "pattern" of poor seasons;

he's not at Forest to be loved, after "hugging" the players too much after defeat.

On top of that, Glasner revealed he refused a request from one of his players to make his own way back to Nottingham from London after the game, banging the table at the press conference when revealing his dismay at that request.

"We have to accept it's not good enough," said Glasner as he walked into the press conference. "If we lose four of the last five games, it's not good enough. And that's why for me, it's now time that we change things, that I change things, and that's what I will do."

Asked what he will change, he replied: "Everywhere, and I feel I could see a few things from day number one. I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it's always compromises.

"It's a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in."

Glasner takes responsibility but points to 'pattern'

Glasner refused to blame his players for the poor start to the season and took full responsibility for the poor set of results.

But he said Forest are in a "pattern" of getting into relegation trouble in recent seasons and wants to change the club from top to bottom.

"I always take responsibility for the things I decided," said Glasner. "I decided everything. It's just one person to blame, and that's me.

"That's why I say I can't and I won't continue in the same way as Oliver Glasner. I will change things. That's so clear for me, because otherwise, again, it's the same.

"You asked the fifth manager, I think you're asking the same question [that you gave to the other four].

"I think the performances are better than the ones [the other four] have been, but it's the same. And if things won't change, you will ask the sixth [manager to come in]."

Asked if he is worried about his future, Glasner said: "I have no consequences. For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family. It's not the worst situation. Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner or with the manager.

"If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won't do it.

"But, you know, the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it's the same, sorry for the word, s*** situation that the club had last year.

"So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises. Zero. Zero. And if these things don't work, they will let me know [about my exit].

"I didn't come to Nottingham because I was bored at home. No, I came to Nottingham to succeed. I came to Nottingham to get the visions of the owner and the fans and the club to reality. And therefore we need to have a bigger change than maybe I thought, to be honest.

"But again, when you're in a club, then you see what's going on. And I'm desperate to get this turnaround. But again, Oliver Glasner can't do anything alone. And I said this so often, and not just after a defeat. I always said the same after winning.

"It's not me, no, we're all together and can do it. But I know where we have to go.And therefore, it's exactly this, being ruthless. And either you buy in or you leave. It's the only way.

"There is no compromise. Either you buy in where we want to go as a club. Because, and I mentioned it, if you're three times struggling, four or five Premier League seasons, struggling, being at the bottom of the league, there is a pattern. And I just know that Oliver Glasner is not here for five years."

'I'm not here to be loved by the players'

Glasner claims Forest have the players to turn their season around - but says he is no longer going to hug them after a disappointment - and that there's a more ruthless way of getting results.

"We have the personnel, but we need to get more out of the players," said Glasner. And this is where I see my responsibility.

"And again, I felt it was more [about] hugging [the players after a defeat]. But if hugging doesn't work, there's also an opposite way.

"And again, I don't need to be loved. I'm here not to be loved. I'm here to bring success to this club. And that's what I think. That's what I will change."

Asked if this could be done overnight, Glasner replied: "No. It's going to take a long time. But in this league and in your position, people will want to see changes immediately.

"Again, I think the club wanted to see changes immediately. That's why they always changed the manager. But the things didn't change.

"Again, I'm an employee. If the leadership thinks I'm the wrong one, they will let me know. But I think things won't change.

"That's just how I see it now. I think I was not harsh enough on getting a few changes."

Glasner reveals he rejected player request to travel alone

In a bid to show unity at the club, Glasner revealed he rejected a request from one of his players to travel back to Nottingham on his own from London.

Instead, the player was forced to join the rest of the squad in taking the three-hour coach.

"I was asked if a player can drive home alone. I said no," Glasner said.

"I have no understanding [why] somebody wants to go home on his own today, from London to Nottingham. No, go with the bus like everybody else. No extras. No extras.

"Buy in. Buy in every single day, every single moment, every single session. Everything we do. You buy in, you can be part of the team.

"You don't buy in? Leave. Otherwise, I'm wrong. I'm in the wrong place."

"He [Glasner] has got a history this guy. It's self-preservation, he just throws his team under the bus. And then he starts digging out about the hierarchy, that's what he is going to do.

"They're not good enough, he's right about that. He's very honest with his appraisal of his side. They are not good enough [but] he's got to get on with it. There is nothing he can do until January. He ain't going to be there in January.

"They will lose next week against Manchester City and he'll get sacked in that international break. They will be on their next manager. Look at the history of this football club, they change managers.

"Marinakis, I quite admire his stance. He gives someone an opportunity - okay people might say he does not give him long enough - but he pulled that club from where they've been to the Premier League and he's made changes along the way.

"He will not have anyone speak out against his football club. And I quite like it, he doesn't sit on his hands and wait, he just makes decisions and he will go and get another manager.

"He's probably saying: 'we spent the money, we brought some new players into the football club, some of them you knew all about and you're not getting the best out of them.'

"The buck stops with the manager and if they can't change personnel at the moment, they need to find someone who can get the best out of them and the position that they find themselves in. In the league, it's not good enough."

articles.title: Man City 0-1 Brighton: Enzo Maresca has issues to address all over the pitch
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca enjoyed a flawless start as Manchester City manager, winning his first seven Premier League games in charge, but the honeymoon period is now over.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca enjoyed a flawless start as Manchester City manager, winning his first seven Premier League games in charge, but the honeymoon period is over.

Having lost at Aston Villa last weekend, City have now suffered back-to-back top-flight defeats after being beaten 1-0 at home by Brighton on Saturday.

"A bit strange," Maresca said of the result. "It is the same feeling as after Aston Villa away. We did enough to deserve something more, but we have to move on and try to win games.

"We created a good volume of offensive action. Sometimes you have to be more clinical and score, but it's important that we create.

"We did everything to be honest. The attitude was good, I have nothing to say about that or the performance. The players fought until the end and hopefully next time we are more lucky."

Maresca seemed to slot in seamlessly after taking on the daunting job of replacing Pep Guardiola, but he now needs to find solutions to City's stuttering form.

With chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano keeping a close eye on proceedings at Etihad Stadium on Saturday, the City manager has issues to address across the pitch.

Brighton stun Man City to maintain bright start

City missed out on the title to Arsenal last season and are expected to be the closest challengers again.

Maresca's men remain top on goal difference but will be overtaken by the Gunners if they avoid defeat at Liverpool on Sunday (kick-off 16:30 GMT).

City have conceded 10 goals in nine league games this term - double the amount that Mikel Arteta's men have let in.

Individual errors at the back are beginning to stack up - Marc Guehi, who was dropped for this game, and Gianluigi Donnarumma were culpable at Villa Park and Matheus Nunes was the guilty party against Brighton .

Maresca has been unequivocal about his number one, saying it is "Donnarumma plus 10" on the teamsheet, but defensive frailties mean City have now kept only one clean sheet in their past eight games in all competitions.

The result also meant City lost consecutive Premier League games for the first time in 14 months.

"Why?" Maresca asked of the individual errors. "Sometimes it happens.

"Unfortunately it is happening for our players, but I think it is part of the game, part of football. It happens many times against us.

"We need to analyse what we can do better and try to move on."

City's midfield was reshaped to the tune of £327m in the summer following the departures of captain Bernardo Silva and 2024 Ballon d'Or winner Rodri.

The incomings included a joint-Premier League record fee of £125m for Enzo Fernandez, £116m on Elliot Anderson and £86m to make Ayyoub Bouaddi the most expensive teenager in English top-flight history.

Maresca, though, seems to still be trying to find the best combination in the middle of the park.

The ex- Chelsea boss usually starts with only two of those summer arrivals behind a number 10, but decided to go with all three and leave Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden on the bench.

"I expected a physical game," Maresca said of his midfield make-up. "Analysing them, watching them, they are aggressive man-to-man. I watched the games they have played.

"I think it was a good idea to start with three physical midfielders and I was also thinking about last 20-30 minutes to refresh with Rayan, Allan and Phil.

"In this moment it is like this and we need just to move on."

Maresca also needs to look at why his side have not been clinical enough in attack in recent games.

Though they have scored 20 goals in nine Premier League games this season, the Brighton fixture ended a run of 23 top-flight games in which City had managed to find the back of the net.

The 21 shots they had on Saturday was the most they have had on goal at home without scoring since 23 attempts against Tottenham in November 2024.

In the past two top-flight games, City have only scored one goal despite managing to create nine big chances.

Against the Seagulls, Erling Haaland was starved of any real service, while Iliman Ndiaye had an off day and missed the best of City's chances in each half.

Maresca added: "I think also in this moment we are the second team in terms of scoring in the Premier League.

"That means we are scoring goals, but in this moment we are conceding silly goals that we can avoid and hopefully we can avoid in the next game."

That comes at RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday, where they will be aiming to return to winning ways.

articles.title: El Tenerife-Andorra, suspendido por la alerta naranja de lluvias
articles.standfirst: El cierre del Heliodoro por parte del Cabildo Insular impide la disputa de la cita programada para este domingo
articles.summary: Mañana, domingo, a las 10.00 horas se sabrá si se juega o no
articles.body: El Tenerife-Andorra, correspondiente a la jornada de este domingo en Segunda, ha sido suspendido debido a la alerta naranja por lluvias decretada en el área metropolitana de Tenerife. El encuentro, previsto para las 20:00 (hora canaria) en el estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López, no podrá disputarse después de que el Cabildo Insular haya anunciado en la tarde de hoy sábado el cierre de las instalaciones deportivas y culturales situadas en las zonas afectadas por el aviso meteorológico. La medida entrará en vigor a partir de las 10.00 horas de este domingo 1 de noviembre y se mantendrá activa hasta que se levanten las restricciones. La decisión responde a la previsión de precipitaciones intensas en el nordeste de Tenerife, donde la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) mantiene un aviso naranja a partir del mediodía. El cierre afecta, además del Heliodoro Rodríguez López, al Pabellón Santiago Martín --en el que juega habitualmente el La Laguna Tenerife--, el Recinto Ferial de Tenerife y el Auditorio Adán Martín. La suspensión de las actividades deportivas en estas instalaciones hace inviable la celebración del encuentro entre blanquiazules y andorranos. La posibilidad de trasladar el partido al lunes, aprovechando el carácter festivo de la jornada, presenta importantes dificultades. Ese día está programado el encuentro del Tenerife femenino frente al Athletic de Bilbao, mientras que el equipo que dirige Álvaro Cervera tiene en el horizonte inmediato su compromiso de Copa del Rey en Badajoz, previsto para este miércoles. Una cita que, además, ya tuvo que ser aplazada la pasada semana como consecuencia del accidente ferroviario. El Tenerife afronta así un nuevo contratiempo en su calendario, pendiente ahora de que se determine una nueva fecha para la disputa del partido frente al Andorra.

articles.title: Alineaciones probables de Racing y Real Madrid para el partido de la jornada 11 de la Liga EA Sports
articles.standfirst: Los blancos regresan a El Sardinero, un campo que no pisan desde 2011
articles.summary: Los blancos regresan a El Sardinero, un campo que no pisan desde 2011
articles.body: El Racing vuelve a recibir a un gigante. Tras años de travesía por el desierto, el conjunto cántabro regresa a Primera División y este domingo (16.15 horas, DAZN) vivirá uno de esos partidos que marcan una temporada entera con la visita del Real Madrid a El Sardinero. Un escenario histórico que vuelve a acoger un Racing-Madrid por primera vez desde 2011. El regreso del equipo verdiblanco tiene además un protagonista especial. Sergio Canales, emblema del racinguismo y uno de los grandes nombres de la plantilla, se medirá al club en el que dio el salto al fútbol de élite. El centrocampista afronta un duelo cargado de simbolismo frente a un Madrid con el que mantiene un vínculo imborrable y ante el que intentará liderar la resistencia cántabra. Llega el equipo de Mourinho en uno de sus mejores momentos de la temporada. El triunfo en el Clásico antes del parón confirmó el crecimiento competitivo de un Madrid que suma cinco victorias consecutivas y que fue capaz de conquistar Barcelona sin Courtois, baja de enorme peso y cuya ausencia parecía poner en jaque la estabilidad defensiva blanca. Sin embargo, el conjunto madridista ha encontrado soluciones colectivas y se presenta en Santander con la confianza por las nubes. Será también un partido inevitablemente marcado por todo lo sucedido esta semana en la gala del Balón de Oro. El fútbol mundial sigue comentando la entrega del premio y el protagonismo de Kylian Mbappé, que terminó segundo en la votación. El delantero francés, principal referencia ofensiva del Madrid y máximo goleador del equipo, tendrá en El Sardinero la primera oportunidad de responder sobre el césped tras una semana de focos, debates y reconocimientos. Y si hay un nombre que explica buena parte del ilusionante regreso del Racing a Primera es el de Zabiri. El delantero atraviesa un momento espectacular y llega a la cita frente al Madrid convertido en la gran referencia ofensiva del equipo cántabro. Sus goles han impulsado al Racing en este inicio de temporada y le han situado entre los atacantes más determinantes de la categoría. Su potencia al espacio, su capacidad para atacar el área y el estado de confianza con el que llega le convierten en una de las principales preocupaciones para la zaga de Mourinho. El Sardinero se aferra a su delantero estrella para desafiar a un Madrid que llega radiante tras conquistar el Clásico. Entre el entusiasmo del Racing por su vuelta a Primera y el excelente momento de forma del Madrid, Santander se prepara para una tarde grande. Un estadio que vuelve a recibir a uno de los gigantes del fútbol español, un Canales dispuesto a desafiar a su pasado y un Mbappé con ganas de convertir en goles el ruido generado por el Balón de Oro. Ingredientes de sobra para uno de los partidos más atractivos de la jornada. Racing: Agirrezabala; Mantilla, Pablo Ramón, Belocian, Aarón Martín; Iván Martín, Almeida; Pablo García, Canales, Iñigo Vicente; Zabiri Real Madrid: Courtois; Dumfries, Konaté, Rüdiger, Carreras; Tchouaméni, Bernardo Silva; Güler, Bellingham, Diomande; Mbappé.

articles.title: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen: Ryan Naderi strikes late to send Gers into Premier Sports Cup final
articles.summary: Report as Rangers book spot in Scottish League Cup final thanks to a late strike from Ryan Naderi
articles.body:
The resilient Dons restricted Derek McInnes's side to one shot on target in a low-quality first half, but the Ibrox side picked up the pace after the break.

Stephen Robinson's side survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute, the big striker redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eight goal of the season which settled the semi-final at Barclays Hampden.

Rangers will face Hearts or Hibernian in the December 13 final, with the Edinburgh sides facing each other at the national stadium on Sunday.

The Govan side went into the game unbeaten in 10 games and firm favourites.

With five Dons defenders missing through suspension or injury - Lewis Mayo, Mats Knoester, Dan Happe, Kristers Tobers and Chris Cadden - there was an element of makeshift about the Aberdeen side, with a first start of the season for Nicky Devlin.

McInnes, who won the trophy with Aberdeen in 2014, raised eyebrows by dropping midfielder Dan Neil, with left-back Tuur Rommens starting and Penrice moving into midfield, and Badredine Bouanani starting in place of Djeidi Gassama.

There was more readjustment for the Dons when Emmanuel Gyamfi injured himself trying to tackle wide-man Kim Min-su and was replaced by former Celtic midfieder Stuart Armstrong, with Brad Lyons moving to right-back.

In the 23rd minute, the Gers defence opened wide open and Nesta Guinness-Walker drove through the gap, forcing goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to tip the shot behind for a corner which came to nothing.

Aberdeen captain Kevin Nisbet glanced a header wide of the goal before Naderi hooked an effort over the crossbar and the game struggled along.

Just before the break, however, Dons goalkeeper Marius Muller parried a decent low drive from Bouanani to safety then Naderi headed a cross from stand-in captain Nico Raskin just over before Kim slashed a drive wide.

As the game stretched, Pandur saved a deflected Kevin Nesbit drive then Muller blocked a shot from Kim before Rangers striker Kevin Kelsy somehow managed to head a pin-point delivery from Bouanani past a post from six yards.

Muller's foot blocked another effort, this time from Bouanani, before Gassama and Neil took over from Kim and Rommens, with Penrice going back to left-back.

The Aberdeen goalkeeper beat away a Raskin volley as the Dons box came under siege and then Bouanani fired wide from the edge of the box.

On a rare break, Nesbit hesitated and his shot was deflected wide by Rangers defender Olwethu Makhanya and from the corner, the Aberdeen striker hooked the loose ball over the bar.

However, the Pittodrie side at last succumbed when Bouanani knocked the ball back to Penrice and he fired towards goal, with Naderi stepping in to beat Muller with a side-footed shot from close range.

articles.title: Roban a Militao durante el Clásico: más de 350.000 euros entre joyas y relojes
articles.standfirst: En su casa, durante el robo, había familiares viendo el partido según informa El Mundo
articles.summary: En su casa, durante el robo, había familiares viendo el partido según informa El Mundo
articles.body: Eder Militao se ha convertido en la última víctima de los robos en casas de futbolistas. El defensa brasileño del Real Madrid sufrió la sustracción de relojes y joyas valoradas en más de 350.000 euros durante el Clásico del pasado domingo, según informa El Mundo. Entre las 21.00 y las 22.00 horas, durante el primer tiempo del partido en el que Militao se quedó en el banquillo, al menos dos individuos se colaron en una de las estancias superiores de la casa del brasileño, en La Moraleja, mientras en el piso inferior varios familiares del futbolista seguían el encuentro. Cuenta El Mundo que "Militao echó en falta un Rolex de 53.000 euros y un Richard Mille de unos 170.000; tres bolsos de Chanel valorados en torno a 15.000 euros; sortijas y pulseras de Cartier por unos 25.000; y más joyas, brazaletes y maletas que elevan la cifra total hasta superar, previsiblemente, los 350.000 euros". Fue la policía la que acudió al domicilio, junto a miembros de la vigilancia privada de la urbanización, puesto que los ocupantes de la casa no se habían dado cuenta de nada. Al inspeccionar la habitación del jugador, se encontraron sus pertenencias revueltas.

articles.title: Nuno Espirito Santo: West Ham United boss says he is 'under pressure every day'
articles.summary: West Ham United head coach Nuno Espirito Santo says he is under pressure every day as West Brom win intensifies criticism of him.
articles.body:
You just know all is not well at a club when your own fans are singing "sacked in the morning" at you.

That fate befell Nuno Espirito Santo as he cut a lone figure on the edge of the West Ham technical area deep into four added minutes at the end of Saturday's dismal 3-1 home defeat by West Brom .

"You only need to write two things: 'West Ham are (bad) and he needs to go'," said one irate fan at the London Stadium as they filed out past the press tribunes.

The Hammers' Halloween horror - which saw the promotion favourites slip to eighth in the Championship table - was punctuated by heated boos at various points, both as the home side spurned chances and gave them up at the other end, while the manner of the three Albion goals were in the spirit of the season - no tricks, just treats.

Asked if he felt his job was under pressure after the game, Nuno replied in bullish fashion: "I am always under pressure. Every day."

The Portuguese does cut a frustrated figure these days. Perhaps understandably, because although he is the one picking the players, he is not the one failing to close down the opposition or allowing them to cross.

He is not losing his man in the box, he is not fluffing a clearing kick underneath his own crossbar, presenting a chance to the opposition to seal the points.

And West Brom were the third visitors in all competitions to have left the London Stadium victorious in the past four games.

Hammers' home horrors continue as Albion march on

On the record, of course, Nuno, projected unity. "All of us are really frustrated," he said.

"There's a lot of explanations - the basics are we didn't play good, we conceded too easy."

All the talk before and after the game was about West Ham's astonishing record of now having fallen behind in 10 of their 16 games in all competitions this season.

Albion's opener was the fourth goal they have conceded in the opening 20 minutes across their past three home league games. They have not managed one of their own in that spell.

Nuno held a meeting with the players about this very topic in the run-up to the game, yet it made no difference.

Despite winning a corner inside 16 seconds, from which Mohamadou Kante hooked a bouncing ball over the bar, they could not get any momentum going.

Arguably the three classiest players on the pitch - with due respect to Jarrod Bowen, who showed his in flashes - were West Brom's Isaac Price, Jimmy-Jay Morgan and Felix Horn Myhre, who combined to give the hosts another mountain to climb.

"It's very concerning we are conceding the first goal on a regular basis," Nuno said. "The message is totally the other way around - the idea is to start the game on the front foot.

"The first moment West Brom get an offensive situation they score. We have to improve on defence and try to score first."

West Ham have conceded six goals in their past two home matches, and they definitely missed Konstantinos Mavropanos in both boxes, with 18-year-old Airidas Golambeckis enduring a tough afternoon alongside the vastly more experienced Max Kilman and Morato.

"We have not been able to play as good as we should," Nuno said. "We are facing good teams but our responsibility is to use the home factor and the support of our fans to win matches."

Defeats by Southampton and West Brom have the Irons playing catch-up to both opponents in the table, and Nuno admitted: "It's very costly for us. We have a clear objective in mind. Every result we don't achieve, we get further away from our objective. It's very difficult."

The one bright point is that Greek defender Mavropanos might just be fit for Wednesday's trip to Cardiff after the knee problem he picked up against Saints.

"He's a very important player for us. He's improving, we are positive," Nuno said.

After a day like Saturday, Nuno will merely hope he is still in position to benefit from his return.
