articles.title: Tottenham 2-0 Crystal Palace: Jean-Philippe Mateta's red card sees 10-man Eagles slip into relegation zone
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Tottenham beat 10-man Crystal Palace for third straight league win; Jean-Philippe Mateta's early red card sees pressure maintained on Palace boss Pierre Sage as Eagles drop into the relegation zone; Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke goals give Spurs win
articles.body:
Jean-Philippe Mateta's 13th-minute red card was followed just 12 minutes later by Archie Gray's headed opener at a corner.

Jan Paul van Hecke's scrappy second-half rebound finish then settled the game to give Spurs three consecutive league wins for the first time since February 2025 and move Roberto De Zerbi's side up to eighth.

But Palace's third league loss in a row, which leaves them third-bottom, came after Mateta was sent off for a late studs-up sliding tackle on Micky van de Ven's Achilles.

Referee Michael Oliver had originally shown a yellow card to the Palace striker, but VAR sent Oliver to the monitor, and he changed his decision to a red for serious foul play.

Not only did the straight red card lead to Palace's defeat, but it leaves them without Mateta for their next three Premier League games - a run which could be crucial in deciding Sage's future as they face Liverpool, Coventry and Hull.

Palace showed plenty of fight and grit for the under-pressure Frenchman at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as Spurs struggled to find a second goal to make the win safe.

But Van Hecke's bundled finish brought relief to the Spurs faithful, who saw their side win back-to-back home league games for the first time since November 2024.

There was nearly more late Spurs joy too, as teenager Luca Williams-Barnett should have had an assist on his Premier League debut after he wonderfully set up Mohammed Kudus, who somehow missed from close range.

Sky Sports News' Chris Reidy at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium:

"The pressure is continuing to grow on Pierre Sage. Every loss now pushes Steve Parish and Crystal Palace decision-makers closer to making a change.

"Since the 5-0 defeat at Brighton, the powers that be have wanted to see defensive improvements in the team and results pick up. Since then they've lost twice in the Premier League, but at least with some improved performances, notably in cup competitions against Besiktas and Fulham.

"Palace weren't expected to win at Spurs, especially after going down to 10 men, but they're now in the bottom three with Liverpool visiting Selhurst Park next Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

"A vulnerability from set-pieces has been a theme under Sage, which again will be a worry for the hierarchy.

"For the second game running, Palace's away support chanted Sage's name; there's an understanding from them he's been dealt a tough hand after losing Maxence Lacroix and Daniel Munoz in the summer. And the players at Spurs certainly didn't show a lack of effort; in fact, it was the opposite, they put in a shift.

"But this is a results business, as Sage has admitted himself, and Parish hasn't been afraid to make ruthless decisions: think back to Patrick Vieira.

"It feels right that Sage should get fixtures against Coventry and Hull to prove himself, but football isn't always so kind. The performances against Fulham in the Carabao Cup and Tottenham tonight have at least shown fight and resilience.

"It's going to be another interesting few days waiting to see if Parish and co stick or twist."

Sage: I'll never give up and have 'rage to train more'

Crystal Palace head coach Pierre Sage speaking at his post-match press conference about their lowly position:

"Yes, it's a disaster for every club in the Premier League, but I have to speak about my club, and I agree with you.

"I'm not comfortable with the situation on the table, but it's a consequence of what we did badly on the pitch, and my only action is on the team and on the pitch.

"But my only way to change things is on the pitch, and that's why I told the players I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday.

"They can trust in me; I will never give up. I will do the best session I can do on Monday because now I have the rage to train more because the game I saw this evening is not in line with my conviction, and I don't like when we let the initiative go to the opponent too much."

On his confidence over whether he will be given time: "It's not me to decide this thing, but if I have one hour, I will give my best during one hour, and if I have 10 years I will give my best during 10 years.

"But you know, for me I'm responsible of the situation, and I am the guy who will find the solution for the situation."

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi speaking at his post-match press conference:

"I'm very happy with the performance because we showed to be a mature team with clear ideas, and we didn't concede a counter-attack, maybe just one in the second half.

"We created many, many chances. If we want to follow the perfection, we have to be more nasty.

"But it's an individual thing, because if I'm the No 9, the No 10, I want to score. But I can't say nothing. We are improving the physical condition.

"(Sandro) Tonali today was unbelievable, incredible. We played with two players more. Tonali was the double today."

Tottenham defender Jan Paul van Hecke speaking with Sky Sports about De Zerbi and the winning run:

"He's a top manager. I have a really good relationship with him.

"That's a big reason why I came here because he gets the best out of me, and I think there's a lot more to come from us.

"When you win games, the confidence grows. When you keep a clean sheet, that also helps.

"Now we need to stay calm and keep going, and we will win a lot of games for sure."

Opta stats: Palace record their lowest PL possession

Crystal Palace have lost 5-0 against Brighton, 2-0 against Newcastle and now 2-0 against Spurs in their last three league games. It's the first time they've lost three in a row without scoring since March 2023.

Spurs had 34 shots in this match - it's the most they've had in a Premier League game since February 2016 (34 vs Swansea), and the most Crystal Palace have faced on record in a game in the competition (since 2004-05).

Spurs had 79.4 per cent possession against Crystal Palace, their second-highest on record (since 2003-04) in a Premier League match (80.2 per cent vs Newcastle in August 2019). Meanwhile, it was Crystal Palace's lowest ever recorded in a Premier League game (20.6 per cent).

Among ever-present sides, Crystal Palace have lost the most games (15) and conceded the most goals (52) of any Premier League side in 2026, while they've also won the joint-fewest games (6) and scored the joint-fewest goals (29) this calendar year.

articles.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Borussia Dortmund: Harry Kane misses penalty and Fabio Silva punishes him in Der Klassiker
articles.summary: Match report and free highlights as Bayern Munich drew 2-2 with Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker. Harry Kane missed a penalty on the night Munich paid tribute to their Ballon d’Or winner as Fabio Silva equalised to have the final say in the Allianz Arena
articles.body:
This was Kane's first appearance since his Ballon d'Or win and he was honoured in Munich before kick-off, making his own entrance separate from the other players, but the game itself turned into a Halloween nightmare for him in the second half.

With Bayern leading through Konrad Laimer's goal, Kane saw his penalty strike the crossbar before Serhou Guirassy levelled the match after the Bayern striker had been dispossessed in the build-up. Even his assist for Dayot Upamecano's goal was not enough.

That is because Silva stepped up off the bench to equalise for Niko Kovac's side in the 89th minute and though Lennart Karl hit the crossbar with the last kick of a dramatic game, Dortmund held on to remain level on points at the top of the Bundesliga table.

It was another Englishman, Jobe Bellingham, who had appeared to open the scoring following a mix-up involving Upamecano. But it was ruled out after a VAR check showed Carney Chukwuemeka colliding with the goalkeeper as Bellingham swept home.

Bayern, who came into this averaging over five goals per home game this season, took advantage immediately when Michael Olise, who had earlier struck the post, sent Laimer through on goal and the Austrian finished at the second attempt.

Dortmund's leveller was a shock given Bayern's dominance but neat work by Guirassy carved out the opening to leave Kane sweating. He looked to have spared his own blushes with a key assist but Silva's intervention made it a night to forget for Bayern's No 9.

This is a difficult period for Bayern with a hectic schedule coming at a time when they are without their recovering head coach Vincent Kompany and a growing injury list. With Luis Diaz already out, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry went off injured in the first half.

Perhaps they will be pleased just to come through this run with their unbeaten record intact but this was an opportunity to open a gap to their great rivals. Silva's strike, with a little help from Kane's rare profligacy, means that their records remain identical instead.

66 - GOAL! Upamecano restored Bayern's lead from Kane's assist

articles.body: Fermín puso ayer sobre el césped del Spotify Camp Nou todo su repertorio: goles, asistencia, intensidad, lucha, pelea... El andaluz firmó, sobre todo, una excelente primera mitad. articles.standfirst: Pol Fortuny y Ciria encarrilan el triunfo del Castilla en los 17 primeros minutos de partido y el filial sigue fuerte en casa
articles.summary: Pol Fortuny y Ciria encarrilan el triunfo del Castilla en los 17 primeros minutos de partido y el filial sigue fuerte en casa
articles.body: Escala puestos en la tabla el Castilla gracias a sus grandes cifras en sus encuentros como local, que le dejan, junto al Nastic, como el mejor conjunto en su feudo. Doce de sus quince puntos se han cocinado en el Di Stéfano, destacando los dos últimos choques en los que ‘los jugones’ han tomado las riendas del equipo para obtener victorias cómodas. La de este sábado ante el Cartagena después de que dos grandes goles de Pol Fortuny y Ciria encarrilasen el triunfo del filial en los primeros 17 minutos de partido. El conjunto blanco no quería sustos un 31 de octubre. Los ‘jugones’ debían devolver a los suyos a la senda de la victoria en lo que viene siendo su verdadero fortín. Si los cartageneros intentaban ahogar la creación en la medular, este once contenía soluciones, y qué soluciones. La movilidad y verticalidad entre los hombres más talentosos llevó a los dos goles con apenas cinco minutos de diferencia que resultaron ser la ventaja definitiva. Pol Fortuny abrió la lata con un gran desmarque a un inmejorable pase en diagonal de Leiva desde la izquierda. Ciria golpeó de nuevo a los albinegros en el 17’ con un golazo tras una carrera poderosa y un golpeo de zurda con fuerza y colocación, no sin antes golpear el balón en ambos palos. Una jugada que ponía distancia y que nacía tras la recuperación en un ataque cartagenero. La solidez en la medular de la dupla aragonesa configurada por Cestero y Roberto Martín, más una actuación sin fisuras de Joan Martínez en la zaga, llevaron al Castilla a no sufrir, salvo por el tanto anulado a Marcos Moreno en el 30’ por falta previa de Ribeiro a Aguado. Los de López de Lerma se encontraron cómodos en la reanudación, ante un Cartagena que decidió buscar minimizar distancias con algo de paciencia y sin precipitación para evitar que el marcador se ampliara. Acumulando saques de esquina intentaron cercar la meta de Javi Navarro, que repitió titularidad, obligando a la defensa blanca a emplearse a fondo. A veinte para el final una gran parada de Javi Navarro evitó el tanto cartagenero a saque de falta directa, aunque el momento de tensión llegó con la revisión solicitada por posible mano de Roberto Martín al remate de Ajenjo, aunque el colegiado no apreció la petición en el 74’. El marcador se mantuvo con la ventaja blanca obtenida en la primera parte, volviendo a dejar la puerta a cero el filial blanco. De Blasis, Jean Jules (84’ Benito Ramírez), Raúl Dacosta (77’ Richarte); Ibán Ribeiro (84’ Marcelo), Marcos Moreno. Entrenador: Iñigo Vélez. Goles: 1-0 (12’): Pol Fortuny; 2-0 (17’): Ciria. Árbitro: Ekaitz Ikiñi García Arriola (C. País Vasco). Amonestó con cartulina amarilla a Dacosta (38’), Jurado (47’), Carvajal (56’), Imanol Baz (66’), Joan Martínez (69’), Roberto Martín (85’), Perejón (87’) y Pol Fortuny (91’). articles.title: Irish Premiership: Has Cliftonville's season finally turned a corner? - Story of the day
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI explores if Cliftonville's emphatic 7-1 win over Carrick Rangers could be a catalyst for improvement in their season.
articles.body:
Cliftonville's recent run of six league defeats with just two goals scored in the process seems like a distant memory now after their emphatic 7-1 victory against Carrick Rangers at Solitude.

The impressive win is the first time that the Reds have scored seven goals in the league in almost 12 years, when they defeated 10-man Ballymena United 7-0 in November 2014, and the side displayed a confidence that has not been on show much this season.

Just two weeks ago, Cliftonville's form was a real concern with manager Jim Magilton under pressure, but now his side have won their past three matches in all competitions and scored 12 goals.

Is this the turning point for the Reds? BBC Sport NI explores some of the signs that it could be the start in a sustained upturn in form.

'So much more to come from Healy' - Magilton

Cliftonville have enjoyed plenty of prolific forwards over recent years with record goalscorer Joe Gormley, Ryan Curran and Liam Boyce among those to have made their mark in north Belfast.

There were hopes that Brian Healy could become the latest name on that list following his January move from H&W Welders, but he struggled to find consistency in his early months at the club.

However, now, he has now scored four goals in his past two games and has shown a confidence and composure that makes him an exciting prospect at the club.

Healy may have had his eyes on the match ball against Carrick after scoring once in each half, but he was substituted on the hour mark with Magilton saying it is key to keep the striker "hungry" ahead of a busy period for the Reds.

"We have a big game Tuesday [against Bangor in the ToalsBet Senior Shield], keep him hungry," Magilton told BBC Radio Ulster's Sportsound.

"During the tough spell there was a lot of criticism both from the outside and inside, but I have great faith in these lads, so it takes time to rebuild, and it takes time for players to settle at a club, particularly a club like ours.

"Brian [Healy] has always had that incredible knack and quality and it was just about giving him that confidence to go and do that and he is repaying that now and there is so much more to come from him."

For Cliftonville, having a confident and in-form Healy leading the line could prove hugely significant as they aim to climb the table.

Healy's performance was not the only stand-out one, with the overall team display something that will please Magilton.

Man of the match Liam McStravick scored the opening goal and brought pace and creativity to the Reds' attacking play, while captain Rory Hale once again demonstrated his ability to deliver important goals with his second in as many games.

Ben Quinn impressed and netted the Reds’ fourth goal and his fifth of the campaign before Rhyss Campbell also made his mark and proved the impact that substitutes can have with his first goals of the season.

The variety of goalscorers is important as Cliftonville had managed just two goals across their previous six defeats, but now look capable of hurting opponents through multiple sources.

The ruthless win was also Cliftonville's first home victory since 5 September when they beat Portadown, which makes the thrashing even more satisfying for the home support who had endured a frustrating few months with the team guilty of squandering big chances and being left to rue them.

Magilton's side have not only recovered from a poor spell, but they have done so in style and in different competitions in recent weeks.

They recorded a narrow Shield win over Glentoran, a comfortable League Cup win over Portadown and a tough league win over the Swifts followed by their big home victory against Stephen Baxter's side.

However, how far the Reds' revival will stretch after they jumped up to fifth in the table, will be tested as they face a busy period of fixtures in multiple competitions in the next few weeks.

As mentioned, they take on Bangor on Tuesday in the Shield semi-final, before a quick turnaround for a home Irish Premiership game against defending champions Larne on Friday.

Their six defeats in a row may have had many fans concerned this would be a challenging season, but if the ruthless Reds maintain their promising form, those fears will become a distant memory.

articles.title: Man City 0-1 Brighton: Bart Verbruggen spreads 'belief' as Seagulls impress
articles.summary: Goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen was the man of the moment on Saturday afternoon as he produced an impressive individual display to help Brighton beat Manchester City
articles.body:
When the full-time whistle sounded at Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon, there was a striking contrast in the emotions of the players from Manchester City and Brighton .

Three days after losing to City on penalties in the Carabao Cup fourth round, the Seagulls achieved a 1-0 victory in the Premier League rematch, bouncing back to underline why they must be taken seriously towards the top of the table this season.

It was no coincidence that most of the Brighton players made a beeline for the outstanding Bart Verbruggen.

The Netherlands goalkeeper made seven saves during a phenomenal afternoon's work to help Brighton not only secure three points but also earn a fifth clean sheet in six Premier League matches.

Verbruggen's finest moment came during the second half when he produced a sprawling save down to his right to keep out a fierce effort from Matheus Nunes and deny City an equaliser.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler commended Verbruggen's display for "spreading belief" as Brighton became the first visiting side to keep a Premier League clean sheet at the Etihad since Tottenham in August 2025.

"It's important to have this mindset and to spread it around the environment we work in, and belief is key to winning these types of games," said Hurzeler.

"Coming here to City, against one of the best teams in the league, is always special. You have to be brilliant at the basics and everyone was contributing.

"From Tuesday, when we travelled [to Manchester], we wanted to have a good four days, enjoy it and finish strong. Everyone can enjoy this win today."

Brighton stun Man City to maintain bright start

There could have very easily been a different outcome.

This was an afternoon when Manchester City accumulated an xG of 1.92, compared to 1.00 for Brighton , so there was no shortage of chances for the hosts.

Home head coach Enzo Maresca will be all too aware that City will have to rediscover their finishing touch - and quickly - if they are to mark his debut campaign in charge with a first Premier League title since 2024.

Manchester City had 21 shots on target without scoring, their highest number without doing so in the Premier League since November 2024, when they managed 24 in a game and drew a blank.

When Maresca sits down to pick apart his side's shortcomings, he will look rueful at chances from Iliman Ndiaye, Abdukodir Khusanov and Nunes in particular.

But to say Brighton 's victory only came because of an off performance from City would be an extreme injustice to Hurzeler's side, who are quickly becoming one of the most well-rounded in the Premier League.

In addition to being the division's highest scorers - having found the back of the net 24 times in nine matches this season - Brighton have also kept the most clean sheets (six).

Only Premier League champions Arsenal - who have played one game less and travel to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday - have conceded fewer goals than Brighton 's seven. Arsenal have shipped five, going into the Liverpool game.

One of the main reasons behind Brighton 's solid rearguard has been the signing of Luka Vuskovic from Tottenham Hotspur .

The 19-year-old has been a transformative figure since arriving at Amex Stadium for a club record fee in July, starting all nine Premier League matches.

The Croatian has formed a rock-solid partnership with fellow centre-back Lewis Dunk and built an understanding with goalkeeper Verbruggen, all of whom played the full 90 minutes at the Etihad.

"It was a good game from all of us," said Verbruggen. "I'm happy to help the team and make some important saves, but I wasn't the only one.

"I think there were four or five shots blocked in an amazing way as well. It was a joint effort from everyone. We celebrate and go again."

Maresca's big test is to address mounting Man City issues

Brighton not getting carried away by title talk

That's the question football supporters up and down the country are asking themselves as Brighton continue to soar up the Premier League table.

The Seagulls sit third, just two points behind Arsenal and Manchester City , and are making a strong case to become the Premier League's most unlikely title challengers since Leicester City, priced at 5,000-1 by bookmakers, achieved the unthinkable in May 2016.

Brighton 's steady rise since returning to the top flight in 2017 means any potential title triumph would come as less of a shock than the feat of Claudio Ranieri's fantastic Foxes.

Saturday's victory over Manchester City followed a 3-0 win against Arsenal in September.

These are results that will only strengthen the belief that something special - whether a first Premier League title or Champions League qualification - could be achieved this season.

Asked by Sky Sports whether his side could challenge for the title, Verbruggen was keen to keep expectations in check.

"We are on game nine, so not really," he said. "We'll take it game by game and see what happens because we have loads of games.

"We are just focusing every day on what's ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season.

"We are happy with the way we are playing – not just the results but the way we are playing, too.

"We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things."

articles.title: Plane Banner Calling for Mike Norvell's Firing Seen in Video, Photo Ahead of FSU vs. Clemson
articles.summary: Florida State fans are fed up with head coach Mike Norvell.
articles.body:
Florida State fans are fed up with head coach Mike Norvell.

As the Seminoles (3-4) endure another difficult season, one fan took to the skies to call for Norvell's firing ahead of Saturday's matchup against Clemson:

Norvell, 45, had a brutal opening to his tenure at the school, going 3-6 in 2020 and 5-7 in 2021. He alleviated a lot of concerns in the two seasons that followed, posting a 10-3 mark in 2022 and a 13-1 mark—and controversial snub from the College Football Playoff—in 2023.

But angst has returned to Tallahassee. Since a 63-3 embarrassment against Georgia in the 2023 season's Orange Bowl, the Seminoles are just 10-21. For a program that was a national power under Bobby Bowden and during parts of the Jimbo Fisher years, that run of mediocrity is unacceptable.

There have already been indications that changes are coming. In September, former athletic director Michael Alford was fired . And FSU president Richard McCullough made it clear in a letter to fans this past week that he understands patience is running thin:

Norvell also made a number of changes in the offseason, with ESPN's Andrea Adelson noting in September that he "hired a general manager, remade his personnel department and got a football budget that is estimated to rank in the Top 20 nationally—well above what Florida State had spent the previous year."

Thus far, those changes have not translated to the sort of success that is expected at Florida State. If the Seminoles don't start stacking wins, the creator of Saturday's banner may get their wish.

articles.title: Funes: "En cuanto llegue esa primera victoria, veremos todo de otra manera"
articles.standfirst: El técnico no esconde que la situación es complicada, pero confía en el talento de su equipo para revertir la dinámica
articles.summary: El técnico no esconde que la situación es complicada, pero confía en el talento de su equipo para revertir la dinámica
articles.body: El entrenador del Málaga, Juanfran Funes, reconoció tras la derrota por 2-1 ante el Real Betis que "cada vez pesa más" no haber ganado aún en las once jornadas ya disputadas de LaLiga EA Sports, pero "en cuanto llegue esa primera victoria, se verá todo de otra manera". En la sala de prensa del Estadio La Cartuja, Funes consideró que esta derrota ha sido "dura por no darle premio a nuestra gente" y confirmó que sus jugadores "lo están pasando mal, pero pelean y han tenido hasta el último minuto la posibilidad de sumar aquí". "Cada vez pesa un poco más no ganar, pero vuelvo a decirlo: el equipo tiene talento y capacidad, sin embargo, argumentarlo ahora en esta dinámica es muy complejo", insistió el técnico granadino en rueda de prensa. "Cuando no llega, o lo vives con desilusión o piensas que en la siguiente ya te toca. Dos buenos resultados lo cambiarán todo y tenemos que buscar que lleguen", recalcó Funes. El técnico malaguista reiteró su visión optimista sobre la situación de su equipo, colista de Primera división, aunque admitió que "cada partido es una 'final' y cada partido que juegas nunca vuelve; ésa es la realidad", si bien cree que "en cuanto se quiten la losa de esa primera victoria, van a llegar muchas más" y lo verán "todo de otra manera". Sobre el Betis, afirmó que este sábado "demostraron por qué son equipo de 'Champions'" y reconoció que al Málaga le "costó entrar en los primeros minutos" en el encuentro, "pero en la segunda mitad" se han "repuesto" y consiguieron "tener opciones" de puntuar. "No hubo premio y estos equipos te castigan. Ha costado mucho llegar hasta aquí para ahora bajar los brazos. Hoy he sentido de qué son capaces mis jugadores", concluyó el preparador malaguista.

articles.title: Are Spurs finally finding elusive consistency under Roberto de Zerbi?
articles.summary: Are Spurs finally finding elusive consistency under Roberto de Zerbi after a third successive Premier League win, asks chief football writer Phil McNulty?
articles.body:
The long wait is over. After almost 21 months, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League games in succession again.

Spurs cruised to victory on Saturday against Crystal Palace , who were reduced to 10 men after 13 minutes when striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for an ill-judged lunge at Micky van de Ven.

It means Tottenham have moved into the dizzy heights of the top half of the table.

Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke scored as Spurs built on a platform established by their first league win of the season at home to Coventry City , then fortified by the outstanding victory at Chelsea - only Spurs ' second league triumph at Stamford Bridge in 36 years.

But the prevailing mood inside the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium before kick-off against Palace, undoubtedly shaped by the past, was that the visit of a struggling side represented a banana skin rather than an opportunity.

Tottenham 's players weren't having that, though. Not a bit of it. Instead, Spurs grasped gratefully at the helping hand offered by Mateta's recklessness to end up convincing winners.

Three straight wins represent riches indeed. The last time this happened for Tottenham was in February 2025, more than 600 days ago.

Three wins is as many as Spurs had in their previous 26 league games combined, in which they drew 10 and lost 13, going back to midway through last season.

And, if a further indicator was needed as to just how poor Spurs have been in recent times, this is the first occasion when they have recorded back-to-back home wins in the league for two years.

This latest sequence represents consistency of the sort that has eluded Spurs in recent years, the previous incarnation being the consistency of regular defeats and two successive 17th-place finishes in the Premier League.

We are witnessing a significant mood shift at Spurs , reflected inside this magnificent arena since the psychological barrier of the vital first league win was crossed against Coventry .

Head coach Roberto de Zerbi told BBC Sport's Match Of The Day: "The passion we showed - we didn't lose the focus, the concentration. We made an incredible reaction when we lost the ball.

"We could have scored more goals, but we created many chances. We have to be more nasty, especially in the last third of the match, especially in the finishing. I'm happy because I knew before this would be a tough game."

De Zerbi pleaded for patience for his big summer acquisitions, with midfield duo Sandro Tonali, a £100m arrival from Newcastle United , and £85m signing Mateus Fernandes, who came from West Ham United, both starting slowly.

While any optimistic verdict on Spurs in recent times always comes with natural caution attached, the expensive pair are now showing signs of why De Zerbi was prepared to pay such prices to make them part of his transformation.

Tonali started to come to life against Coventry City and here he was pivotal with his running power, physicality and creation. Fernandes was lively throughout, always looking for the opening, the pass that could make a difference.

And once again, to the usual rapturous reception after his long injury absence, Dejan Kulusevski delivered a lively cameo as substitute, a real threat as he also forced a fine save from Palace keeper Dean Henderson.

There is a sense that something is finally stirring at Spurs , that the £300m spent in the summer might just reap a reward – as you would expect for such a lavish outlay.

The statistics confirmed Spurs ' superiority, although Crystal Palace battled gamely with their numerical disadvantage, never looking like a side who had given up on head coach Pierre Sage, although he will now come under increasing scrutiny as they lie in the bottom three with only two wins from nine league games.

Spurs had 34 shots and faced just two, the biggest shot difference (32) they have had against any opponent since such Opta records began in 2003-04.

It is also the biggest for any side since Liverpool had 36 shots against four from Wolverhampton Wanderers in May 2024.

Spurs also had 79.4% possession, their second highest on record in a Premier League match after they had 80.2% against Newcastle United in August 2019.

Spurs pile pressure on Sage as 10-man Palace are beaten

It all left De Zerbi delighted as he talked with renewed optimism and ambition, saying: "Listen, we are Tottenham . We can't forget to be ambitious, to be hungry, to win games in a row, and to make our fans happy.

"At the same time, we can't forget two weeks ago where we have been in the table, to change the last two to three seasons of this club. Three games in a row is not enough. We have to keep this behaviour, this spirit. This condition to prepare every game in the same way.

"After the international break, we spoke together honestly, and decided to change the mood quickly because in football, you can't ask for time, especially if you have good players like we have. I think nothing has changed, but the mood, spirit, the relationship with the players are totally different."

The mood has shifted and - for now - the curve looks to be moving in an upward direction for Spurs and De Zerbi.

articles.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado vs. K-State Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Led by head coach Deion Sanders, the Colorado Buffaloes finally secured their first Big 12 win of the season on Saturday with a 27-24 overtime victory over the Kansas State Wildcats at Folsom Field in Boulder, Colorado.
articles.body:
Led by head coach Deion Sanders, the Colorado Buffaloes finally secured their first Big 12 win of the season on Saturday with a 27-24 overtime victory over the Kansas State Wildcats at Folsom Field in Boulder, Colorado.

Favored by 2.5-points (h/t FanDuel Sportsbook ) despite entering the game with a mark of 2-5 overall and 0-4 in conference play, Colorado moved into a tie with K-State in the Big 12 standings at 1-4.

Here is a look at the top statistical performers on offense for both Colorado and Kansas State from Saturday's contest:

The Wildcats were without Avery Johnson, who is among the best dual-threat quarterbacks in the country. With Johnson missing the game due to injury, Dillon Duff got the start, but head coach Collin Klein mostly used Blake Barnett.

After a slow start for both offenses, Colorado got on the board first late in the first quarter when running back Richard Young scored a rushing touchdown from two yards out:

The Buffs were on the verge of extending their lead to 14-0 in the second quarter, but disaster struck during a dynamic run by DeKalon Taylor.

Taylor scampered 30 yards and appeared set to score a touchdown, but he was stripped of the ball at the goal line by cornerback Kaleb Patterson and fumbled the ball into the end zone for a touchback:

Kansas State quickly took advantage of that huge defensive play by driving 80 yards in 11 plays, culminating in a 28-yard touchdown pass from Barnett to wide receiver Josh Manning:

That tied the score at 7-7 before halftime and gave the Wildcats a ton of momentum entering the break.

Colorado and Kansas State traded punts coming out of the half until the Buffaloes got back in the end zone late in the third quarter on a 47-yard run by JaQuail Smith:

That score seemed to energize the K-State offense, which tied the score back up at 14-14 just over two minutes later on a 33-yard touchdown strike from Barnett to tight end Linkon Cure:

The Colorado rushing attack continued to roll on the ensuing drive with Young scoring his second touchdown of the day on the ground to restore the Buffaloes' seven-point lead with 12:27 remaining in regulation:

Colorado seemed poised to win the game in regulation, but it was unable to run out the clock on offense and had to punt the ball back to Kansas State with less than a minute left.

Barnett impressively moved the Wildcats down the field with swiftness and threw the game-tying touchdown on a jump pass to tight end Garrett Oakley with two seconds left:

Klein flirted with going for two, but instead settled for the standard extra point to send the game to OT.

After a Kansas State field goal on the first overtime possession, Colorado won it with an 11-yard touchdown pass from Isaac Wilson to Charlie Williams on a third-and-9 play:

With the win, Colorado snapped a five-game losing streak and inched closer to bowl eligibility.

Kansas State fell to .500 on the year, and it has now lost two games in a row and four of its past five following a 3-0 start to the campaign.

Colorado will try to run the winning streak to two next Saturday when it goes on the road to face Arizona State, while K-State is set to host quarterback Drew Mestemaker 24th-ranked Oklahoma State next Saturday.

articles.title: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham: Zion Suzuki concedes own goal as Nicholas Jackson scores after John McGinn's penalty miss in draw with Fulham
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Aston Villa are held to a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham
articles.body:
Villa should have gone ahead after 15 minutes when they were awarded a penalty following a review when Sander Berge was penalised for a handball in the box as he jumped with Leon Goretzka at a corner.

With neither Emi Buendia nor Ross Barkley in the line-up, John McGinn stepped up to take the penalty but the Scotland international - who had only ever taken a penalty for Villa in a shoot-out - smashed the ball against the crossbar and over.

The home side nearly paid a heavy price for McGinn's miss straightaway after a Fulham counter-attack, but Oscar Bobb was brilliantly denied the opener by a one-handed save from Suzuki who tipped the ball over.

Villa went in front after Timothy Castagne's error allowed Johan Manzambi to play a ball through to Jackson, who cut inside and beat David Affengruber, before wriggling clear of the recovering Castagne to slide the ball past Bernd Leno.

There were chances at both ends in the second half, with Victor Lindelof almost extending Villa's when he directed Ian Maatsen's effort towards goal only to be denied by a reflex save from Leno.

Suzuki was forced to divert a Matty Cash away from the on-rushing Gonzalo Garcia before saving an Alex Iwobi header from eight yards out.

But Villa's goalkeeper made an unforced error when he allowed an Iwobi corner to slip through his fingers and bounce over the goal-line before he could retrieve it as Fulham drew level.

Suzuki got down at his near post to make a late save to deny Antonee Robinson, before Pau Torres headed wide from 12 yards out at the other end as both sides had to settle for a point apiece.

Emery: 'Disappointing result but a fair result'

"It was a disappointing result, but a fair result. I think they deserved it as well, this draw.

"It was tough for us in the second half, more than the first half.

"Second half, we knew we should try to play in the same way as in the first half, but they dominated more in the second half, they created chances and they scored a goal.

"We created some chances and we could have even won the match, but I think it was a fair result.

On Suzuki's error: "This is part of football.

"I think he played fantastic and he did a lot of saves and action defensively, so he can make one mistake like this. It's part of football.

Arbeloa: We are a difficult team to beat

"I am so happy with our performance in the second half. This is what I want to see from my team, that character, that ambition.

"We needed to be aggressive against a team like Villa.

"It was a Champions League team in front of us.

"Technically, I thought we were very good but this is the Premier League and you have to be aggressive, and physically, you have to be at your best level.

"I think maybe we deserved a little bit more, but the performance was really great.

"I think we are a very difficult team to beat and I think we can beat anyone."

Fulham are heading in the right direction

There was something rather telling about the reaction of the Fulham players to their travelling supporters at full-time. This was not a team celebrating a point like they had got away with something. It was a team that knew they had given their fans plenty to shout about.

Fulham were excellent for large parts of their 1-1 draw at Aston Villa. They took the game to Unai Emery's side, dictated the tempo for long spells and created enough opportunities to leave Villa Park feeling they should have taken more.

The underlying numbers reinforce the eye test. Fulham generated 2.2 expected goals, the fifth-highest total recorded by any visiting team at Villa Park since the start of the 2023/24 season. They also registered 40 touches inside the Villa penalty area. That is serious territorial dominance against a side who rarely allow opponents to dictate terms on home soil.

This feels like a Fulham team beginning to find its feet. There is more purpose to their attacking play, more conviction in possession and a growing belief that they can compete with the division's better sides.

articles.title: Indiana's Josh Hoover Benched by Curt Cignetti vs. Minnesota, Box Score Stats, Highlights & Reaction
articles.summary: Indiana might have a quarterback problem. It didn't keep the Hoosiers from picking up another win, albeit in dramatic fashion.
articles.body:
Indiana might have a quarterback problem. It didn't keep the Hoosiers from picking up another win, albeit in dramatic fashion.

Head coach Curt Cignetti benched Josh Hoover in favor of Grant Wilson at halftime of the Hoosiers' matchup against Minnesota on Saturday, though the defending champions ultimately prevailed in overtime, 23-16, after a wild sequence of 60-yard field goals forced some extra football.

Here's what Hoover's stats looked like at the time of his benching:

And here are the remainder of the key stats from Saturday's matchup:

Hoover took a big hit late in the first half after throwing an interception, which resulted in a penalty against Minnesota:

It's been a rough stretch for Hoover. Two weeks ago he finished 20-of-40 for 296 yards and a touchdown in a 19-15 loss against Ohio State. Last week he was just 8-of-18 for 81 yards and an interception in a 13-6 overtime win against Michigan.

He carried a probable designation throughout the week.

As for the remainder of the game, it was mostly a defensive affair until a wild finish.

Nick Marsh scored the opening touchdown of the game in the first quarter:

But Minnesota took the lead in the second quarter with a smooth flea flicker:

The Golden Gophers also impacted the game on special teams, blocking a field goal in the second quarter. It was a rough kicking day for Indiana in general—the Hoosiers also fumbled the snap on what would have been a game-tying attempt in the fourth quarter:

Minnesota kicker Luke Drzewiecki, meanwhile, had himself a day, going 3-for-3 on field goals, including a 60-yarder that ultimately served as the game-winner. And yet... tasked with hitting a 60-yarder himself to keep Indiana alive, Paddy McAteer responded as time expired to force overtime.

Charlie Becker then showed up in overtime in a big way, hauling in a touchdown reception on the first play.

Indiana's defense stopped the Gophers on their possession and the upset bid was averted.

For Minnesota (5-3), it was a heartbreaking result after an incredibly valiant effort on the road. For Indiana (8-1), it was a true test of resiliency, even if the questions about Hoover's starting status will linger into the future.

articles.title: Brian Fariñas, un debut sin complejos y con mensaje de Flick
articles.standfirst: El mediocentro de Benicarló se estrena en al elite en el Spotify Camp Nou
articles.summary: El mediocentro de Benicarló se estrena en al elite en el Spotify Camp Nou
articles.body: Hansi Flick recurrió esta noche a la cantera para confeccionar el once ante las lesiones. El técnico culé afrontó el encuentro de LaLiga contra el Alavés con seis bajas por distintas dolencias, cuatro de ellas en defensa: Roony, Olmo, Christensen, Koundé, Eric García y Xavi Espart. Tenía opciones en la primera plantilla, pero apostó por Brian Fariñas para el lateral derecho y por Joao Cancelo en el izquierdo. Reubicó al joven centrocampista de Benicarló, de 20 años, dejando a Alejandro Balde en el banquillo y trasladándole un duro mensaje: ni con una plaga de ausencias cuenta con él para ser titular. Brian Fariñas se estrenó esta jornada en la elite. Lo hizo en el Spotify Camp Nou y en la décima convocatoria con los de Flick. El mediocentro de Benicarló, que llegó a La Masia en verano de 2018 procedente del fútbol base del Villarreal, se suma a la amplia lista de jóvenes del fútbol base a los que el técnico alemán asciende: Marc Bernal, Gerard Martín, Dro, Jofre Torrents, Xavi Espart... El canterano, que luce el dorsal 4, salió de lateral derecho, posición en la que Flick ya le probó durante la pretemporada, en el amistoso contra el Birmingham City. Prefirió moverle antes de confiar en Alejandro Balde: puso a Cancelo en la izquierda. Fariñas tuvo delante a Abderrahman Rebbach, al que no perdió ojo. El joven profesional frenó bien las subidas de los jugadores del Alavés por su banda, sobre todo las del argelino, intentó conectar con Lamine y se asoció bien, especialmente, con Cubarsí y Rodri. También se atrevió a ganar metros y subir al ataque. Se ofreció, habló con sus compañeros de forma constante y sin complejos. Dio 106 pases acertados, y sólo falló cuatro. Firmó un buen encuentro. Para el partido de esta noche contra el Alavés, Flick citó también por primera vez al joven lateral Guillem Víctor y al medio Tunkara. Pero aún deben esperar para su estreno en la elite. Igual que Àlex Campos.

articles.title: Un error garrafal de Suzuki regala un punto a Arbeloa en el derbi con Emery
articles.standfirst: El Aston Villa sigue cerca de Europa y el Fulham continúa fuera del descenso
articles.summary: El Aston Villa sigue cerca de Europa y el Fulham continúa fuera del descenso
articles.body: El derbi en los banquillos entre Unai Emery y Álvaro Arbeloa acabó en tablas. El Fulham sacó un valioso empate -volvió a dejar buenas sensaciones- de su visita al Aston Villa (1-1). Un empate que deja a los 'villanos' novenos con 12 puntos, a tres de Europa; y sitúa decimoquintos a los 'cottagers' con nueve, dos por encima del descenso. Empezó mejor el Aston Villa, que alineó de inicio a Pau Torres. Pudo adelantarse, de hecho, en el 16', después de que el VAR validara un penalti por manos de Sander Berge tras un cabezazo de Goretzka. Sin embargo, John McGinn falló desde los 11 metros: lo estrelló en el larguero, como Kane. El Fulham, con Gonzalo García de titular, fue cogiéndole el 'pulso' al partido. Suzuki se inventó una parada inverosímil en el 32' para salvar un mano a mano con Bobb después de una contra conducida por Robinson. El que no perdonó fue Nico Jackson en el 39'. El ex del Villarreal recibió en profundidad de Manzambi, encaró a Affengruber y Castagne y, cuando más difícil parecía, se abrió hueco para batir a Leno. Suzuki evitó que el Fulham empatara justo antes del descanso al desbaratar un mano a mano con King tras un buen pase filtrado por Gonzalo. La historia se repitió nada más salir del descanso: Suzuki desvió lo justo para que Gonzalo no impactara bien un centro de Robinson. En el 54', más de lo mismo. Esta vez fue un compañero, Shea Charles, el que provocó que Gonzalo terminara rematando alto, con el hombro, en boca de gol. Para colmo, pudo llegar el 2-0 del Villa. Leno atrapó 'in extremis' un tiro de Maatsen que golpeó en Pau Torres. La respuesta de los de Arbeloa, dominadores, no se hizo esperar. Suzuki sacó un remate a quemarropa de Iwobi y Lindelöf desvió a córner el posterior remate de Gonzalo en el 64'. Parecía que no había manera, pero el 1-1 acabó llegando de la manera más inesperada: Suzuki acabó 'palmeando' contra su propia portería el saque de esquina botado por Iwobi. Se 'rehizo' Suzuki con una parada a Robinson en el 80' tras una apertura de Gonzalo. Las dos más claras, sin embargo, las tuvieron los pupilos de Emery... en la cabeza de Pau Torres. El ex del Villarreal remató fuera un gran pase de Cash en el 84' y volvió a cabecear ligeramente desviado una falta lateral botada por Buendía. Al final, un punto para cada equipo en el 'derbi' entre Emery y Arbeloa.

articles.title: El Zaragoza resucita de entre los muertos otra vez y salva un milagroso empate contra otro filial
articles.standfirst: Como ante el Atlético Madrileño, dos goles en el tramo final dejan sin liderato en solitario al Villarreal B
articles.summary: Como ante el Atlético Madrileño, dos goles en el tramo final dejan sin liderato en solitario al Villarreal B
articles.body: El Villarreal B ganaba 0-2 en el minuto 85 en el Ibercaja Estadio y disfrutaba de una tranquila noche de Halloween. Fue entonces cuando el Real Zaragoza resucitó de entre los muertos para marcar dos goles y salvar un punto. Otra vez al final y de nuevo contra un filial como hizo ante el Atlético Madrileño. Los García, Alberto y Álvaro, adelantaron a los castellonenses y Jardí y Diego González, en el descuento, firmaron las tablas. Los de David Albelda ya habían demostrado no temer ningún escenario ni rival y salieron sin miedo. La primera media hora fueron los dueños del balón y de las llegadas más peligrosas. Barattucci de falta tuvo la más clara aunque en varias contras merodearon el primero. De hecho, llegaron a marcar pero fue anulado por fuera de juego. Antes también reclamaron un penalti por mano de Iranzo que no fue. Los blanquillos, que solo habían tenido un cabezazo de Diego González, despertaron en tramo final con otro testarazo del central al larguero y un remate de Jardí que sacó bien Kinareikin. Todo quedaba muy abierto para la segunda mitad. El zaragocismo esperaba otro Real Zaragoza pero nada cambió. El filial del Villarreal continuaba sembrando el pánico con cada llegada. Cheikh marcaba pero el línea volvía a anularlo, pero el gol amarillo era cuestión de tiempo. Y así fue. Gaitán la puso con música y Alberto García no perdonó en el mano a mano. Poco después, fue Eneko el que centró de forma maravillosa y Álvaro García, de volea, definió por la escuadra. La derrota asomaba entre el público blanquillo pero un penalti de Eze a Saidu abría la esperanza. Jardí lo falló pero el rechace lo mandó a la red. Y como este equipo nunca se rinde, aprovechó en el descuento un error del meta rival, impecable hasta entonces, para igualar el choque de cabeza. Tobajas fue expulsado por doble amarilla tras reanudar el juego y el encuentro terminó. Reparto de puntos que mantiene a ambos empatados a puntos en lo alto de la clasificación. articles.title: Colorado storms field after notching first Big 12 win in over a year with OT victory against 4-4 Kansas State
articles.summary: Colorado's win moves the Buffaloes to 3-5 on the year.
articles.body:
The Colorado Buffaloes beat the Kansas State Wildcats in overtime on Saturday afternoon. Seconds after the win, the goalposts came down, and fans began rushing the field.

Colorado's victory moved the school to 3-5 overall, but it was the Buffaloes' first Big 12 win of the season, and their first since Oct. 11, 2025. It also snapped a five-game losing streak and marked Colorado's first win at Folsom Field since Sept. 12, when it beat Weber State 52-21.

To add to the fun, the overtime win came on Halloween. So not only are students pouring onto the field, but costumed students are too, making for quite the visual.

It looked like Colorado would win in regulation, but Kansas State scored a touchdown with two seconds left. The Wildcats lined up for two, but the Buffaloes called a timeout. Kansas State kicked the extra point after it to send the game to overtime.

The Wildcats got the ball first and settled for a field goal. Colorado clinched the win as quarterback Isaac Wilson rifled a pass to tight end Charlie Williams for an 11-yard score.

The Buffaloes have tied their win total from last season. This is the fourth season of the Deion Sanders era at Colorado. So far, the Buffaloes have eclipsed four wins just once, when they finished 9-4 in 2024, the final season of Shedeur Sanders and Travis Hunter's collegiate careers.

Colorado has four games left this season and needs to win three to become bowl-eligible. The Buffaloes play Arizona State next week, then face No. 18 Houston, Cincinnati, and UCF.

All of these are conference games, so Colorado will have four more chances to add to its league win total. One more win this season would mark the second time in the Sanders era that the Buffaloes have won at least two conference games.

The loss drops the Wildcats to 4-4 overall, with a 1-4 record in the Big 12. Kansas State will end the season with games against No. 24 Oklahoma State, TCU, No. 22 Arizona, and Iowa State.

articles.title: Quique Sánchez Flores: "Asumo la derrota, y hoy más que nunca estoy al lado de mis jugadores"
articles.standfirst: El preparador madrileño ofrece su visión del encuentro en el Spotify Camp Nou
articles.summary: El preparador madrileño ofrece su visión del encuentro en el Spotify Camp Nou
articles.body: Quique Sánchez Flores se refirió este sábado al cruce de LaLiga entre el Barcelona y el Alavés disputado en el Spotify Camp Nou. El conjunto vasco sigue sin ganar a domicilio y cayó goleado en el feudo culé. Derrota "Tengo la sensación que en cada acción que iba a gol, lo fue. No fuimos duros ni contundentes. Pedimos disculpas. Como entrenador asumo la derrota, y más que nunca estoy al lado de mis jugadores". Barça "Cuando te imaginas un partido contra el Barça, te imaginas este partido. Les hemos abierto la puerta, les hemos dado facilidades. No hemos sido contundentes. No hemos tenido agresividad y no les hemos incomodado. Hacer menos falta que el rival es un problema. Tuvimos opciones tras el 2-0, tuvimos acercamientos. Pero luego ya nos condenaron los otros dos goles. Nos levantaremos". Goleada "Han hecho el partido que querían. Han controlado el partido. Cada vez que nos tiraron, nos hicieron gol. Nos vamos frustrados. Quiero que la crítica recaiga en el entrenador, no en mis jugadores". Daño "Deja huella. Hay que saber que pudimos ser mejores, pero esto es pasajero. No podemos quedarnos en el error, hay que pasar página. Son rachas que no se pueden permitir, pero pueden pasar. Hay que saber qué hemos hecho mal y solucionarlo". Agresividad "Están cansados, agotados, han intentado cerrar los espacios... no nos ha faltado ganas o intención, pero nos hemos equivocado. Si no hay intensidad, el entrenador debe recapacitar".

articles.title: Rangers: McInnes demands more after delivering trophy chance
articles.summary: Derek McInnes knows there is room for improvement as he steers in-form Rangers to the Premier Sports Cup final with a 1-0 win over Aberdeen.
articles.body:
Rangers manager Derek McInnes stands a final away from delivering a first major trophy in charge at Ibrox, at the first time of asking, after Ryan Naderi's late winner overcame stubborn Aberdeen at Hampden Park.

Either Hearts or Hibernian will be the opponents come December as the former Hearts, Kilmarnock and Aberdeen boss seeks just his second major trophy after over 800 matches in various dugouts.

Yet, overseeing a turnaround in form that has culminated in an 11-game unbeaten run doesn't seem to have left McInnes completely content as he called for more from his side despite taking another significant step in a season that offers increasing promise.

It's perhaps a measure of what he sees is required to succeed at a club so starved of consistent silverware. A reminder that standards aren't where he wants them to be.

Naderi goal puts Rangers into League Cup final at expense of Aberdeen

The Ibrox side have enjoyed an impressive seven clean sheets during this unbeaten run. That's been the bedrock, with Olwethu Makhanya performing consistently at centre-half. Another shutout against Aberdeen went a long way given their inability to convert chances.

Rangers had 74% possession in their semi-final win. They had 25 shots on goal but just five on target until Naderi tapped home on 83 minutes.

"The job was to get the team and the club into a cup final and it's job done by hook or by crook," McInnes told BBC Scotland.

"The stats will show possession, 25 shots, but to only have five shots on target isn't good enough.

"Those stats are similar to what we see most weeks in terms of not enough shots on target and it's bad decision-making.

"It's such an important goal for us to get into the final but we do need to improve.

"Hopefully between now and then [the final] we can keep winning games but there has to be an obligation from all of us to try and get better performances."

Arriving from the German third tier in February, Naderi cut an unconvincing figure last season with many doubting his credentials to lead the line for Rangers.

His Hampden winner adds to his collection of vital goals, having scored in the 1-0 league win at Celtic Park.

His tally of eight goals is a good return but also his impact overall, in the absence of Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti, has contributed significantly to Rangers' rise.

"Naderi is just a man that is completely transformed this season," former Ibrox midfielder Andy Halliday insisted.

"Not only is he complimenting that work ethic that's always been there but with goals and effectiveness at the top end of the pitch, it's that man again who comes up with the goods."

Again, though, his manager believes the Czech Republic forward can offer more if the team play to his strengths.

"He is a bit of a parasite in the sense that he thrives off service," McInnes explained.

"We just need to put more balls in the box for him but balls with a bit more quality. He's been a big game player for us already this season."

The demand at Rangers is clear. Win trophies. It's something that simply hasn't happened anywhere near enough in recent times, with just three delivered since 2012.

"We know the importance of getting to finals time and time again," McInnes said.

"This needs to be our norm year in year out, that we arrive at Hampden and we put ourselves in a position to lift silverware.

"If you don't win this [the semi-final] then question marks hang over and it's hard to keep the the noise quiet.

"It gives the supporters something to look forward to, it keeps a feel-good factor about the club.

"I think every team has got the ability to improve and I certainly feel that way with this team."

articles.title: Dylan Raiola Impresses, Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Oregon Win vs. Northwestern
articles.summary: Dylan Raiola led Oregon to a comeback win over No. 20 Northwestern in his fifth appearance as an injury replacement for Dante Moore.
articles.body:
Dylan Raiola led Oregon to a comeback win over No. 20 Northwestern in his fifth appearance as an injury replacement for Dante Moore.

The Ducks trailed until the fourth quarter of Saturday's home game before storming back to claim a 34-26 victory.

Here's a look at the top performers that helped Oregon improve to 5-3 on the season.

Oregon fell into an early 20-6 deficit after allowing Northwestern to score on each of their first four drives.

Raiola responded in the second quarter by finding Dakorien Moore for a short touchdown pass to cut the disadvantage to seven points.

The Ducks' opening possession of the second half ended when Northwestern's Braydon Brus recovered a fumble lost by Moore.

Oregon's defense forced Northwestern to punt on their final drive of the third quarter before Raiola made a 17-yard touchdown pass to Jamari Johnson to give the Ducks their first lead of the game.

Moore added to that lead by running in a 75-yard touchdown on the first play of the Ducks' next drive.

Oregon's defense closed out the win as Northwestern's final two offensive drives ended in a missed 42-yard field goal attempt and a three-and-out.

Raiola is eligible to declare for the 2027 NFL draft, but he could hope to succeed Moore as Oregon's full-time starter and delay his entry until 2028. He was not listed on Bleacher Report's most recent 2027 NFL draft big board .

Moore suffered his season-ending concussion in a Sept. 26 matchup against USC.

Raiola has recorded an up-and-down season since that date. He was benched in his first start of the season against UCLA, then stepped in for Brock Thomas to throw a game-winning touchdown against Nebraska.

This marks Raiola's second straight start after also getting the nod last week against Illinois. He could face his biggest test of the season so far at No. 2 Ohio State next Saturday.

articles.title: Bears Could Make Another Major Trade After Jeffery Simmons Move
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears made the biggest splash of the trade season so far when they landed All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans on T...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears made the biggest splash of the trade season so far when they landed All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans on Thursday — and they might not be done.

However, their next move could be a surprising one.

With the Nov. 10 trade deadline fast approaching, The Ringer's Tom Pelissero believes it would make sense for the Bears to at least field calls on All-Pro cornerback Jaylon Johnson.

"It's unlikely the Bears will end up moving Johnson, who is in his seventh season in Chicago and sixth as a starter," Pelissero wrote. "But with Kyler Gordon making an impact since his return from injury and the team's financial picture in flux after the Simmons trade, it would make sense to listen to calls.

"Johnson, 27, is due about $9.697 million for the rest of this season, including active roster bonuses, and $16 million in 2027 with no guarantees."

The Bears are a long shot to move the two-time Pro Bowler, but stranger things have happened at the deadline. Look no further than last year when the New York Jets shocked the league when they shipped Pro Bowler Sauce Gardner to the Indianapolis Colts for two first-round picks.

Bears CB Jaylon Johnson Hasn't Looked Like a Pro Bowler

It's not hard to see why the Bears would at least pick up the phone on Johnson.

Chicago's defense has been one of the better units in the league, ranking eighth in total yards allowed (313.4 per game), third in rushing yards allowed (87.6) and ninth in points allowed (20.4) through seven weeks. However, the pass defense is a different story.

The secondary has struggled for three straight games, and Johnson has been arguably the biggest culprit. He's allowed a passer rating of 100.4 or worse in every game this season and a 129.4 rating overall, according to Pro Football Reference. His seven missed tackles are also a team high.

Two of those misses came on touchdowns in last week's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots . Drake Maye faked him out on a run, and Rhamondre Stevenson turned a short pass into a 48-yard catch-and-run.

Head coach Ben Johnson didn't exactly offer a vote of confidence when he was asked about the two-time Pro Bowl CB this week.

"There's been some ups and some downs, and so just like everybody we're evaluating at the end of each game, winning performance versus losing performance," Johnson said . "And like I alluded to with Daniel Hardy , he's a prime example, guys that are stepping up in their opportunities, they warrant more playing time.

"And so that's the case that we do offense, defense, and special teams each and every week, and we'll continue to do that."

Why the Bears Could Cut Ties With Jaylon Johnson

Johnson is just two years removed from back-to-back Pro Bowls, including a second-team All-Pro nod in 2023, which earned him a four-year, $76 million extension in March 2024.

But groin surgery cost him 10 games last season, and he hasn't looked like the same player since. The lack of guaranteed money in 2027 is what makes him movable.

The Bears would free up $16 million next offseason by moving on from him, which could come in handy after taking on Simmons' three-year, $105.8 million extension. Johnson himself called 2026 "definitely a contract year" back in training camp.

Still, with Simmons in the fold and the Bears looking like legitimate contenders, general manager Ryan Poles doesn't have to sell. However, if someone makes an offer he can't refuse, it wouldn't surprise anyone if Johnson's time in Chicago comes to an end next week.

articles.title: Florida QB Aaron Philo benched for Tramell Jones Jr. after 2 first-half interceptions vs. Georgia
articles.summary: Philo's first pick came off an egregiously bad throw on the run, leading to a touchdown for the Bulldogs.
articles.body:
Florida quarterback Aaron Philo was benched after throwing a pair of interception early in Saturday's matchup between the No. 17 Gators and No. 3 Georgia. After Philo's picks led the Bulldogs to a 10-0 lead in the second quarter, head coach Jon Sumrall opted to put in sophomore quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. as QB1.

Philo, who was back as starting quarterback after a brief absence with a shoulder injury, did not get things started on a good note. The junior QB ended his opening drive in the first quarter with a baffling interception on the run.

On third-and-6, Philo faced pressure from the Bulldogs' defensive line, and was forced to scramble around before he lost his footing. But Philo, as he went down, decided to fling the ball into the air — where it was easily picked off by Georgia defensive back Ellis Robinson IV.

Georgia, which opened the game with a missed field goal that went well right, initially looked like it wouldn't be able to convert Philo's gift of a turnover into points. But on fourth-and-15, Gators cornerback Javier Jones took out the legs of Bulldogs punter Drew Miller, causing a roughing the kicker penalty that gave Georgia the first down.

With the drive kept alive, the Bulldogs went on to score a touchdown, taking a 7-0 lead thanks to some awful mistakes from Florida.

After a three-and-out Gators drive, Philo then went on to throw another first-half pick, with the ball slipping through the hands of his receiver and into the hands of Georgia DB Demello Jones.

Despite the great field position, the Bulldogs had to settle for a field goal to grow the lead; kicker Peyton Woodring, who missed the earlier attempt, successfully hit the 28-yarder.

Tramell Jones Jr. then replaced Philo on the next drive, but didn't fare much better. On Jones' second drive of the game, a strip sack led the sophomore to fumble, letting Georgia pick up a scoop-and-score touchdown to make it 24-0.

In the third quarter, Jones finally got Florida within a few yards of the end zone, but threw an interception that was wrangled in by DB Braylon Conley.

Though Jones did eventually score a touchdown in the fourth quarter, taking the two-yard rush himself to break up the shutout. But it wasn't enough to stave off the Bulldogs, who got the win after a dominant defensive showing.

Philo sat out the Gators' 27-24 upset win over Georgia two weeks ago with an injury to his throwing shoulder, leaving backup Tramell Jones Jr. to earn his first career start, but returned Saturday after Florida's bye week.

On Saturday, Jones finished 18-for-25 on passing, taking four sacks.

articles.title: Premier League: Coventry, Ipswich, Hull - promoted trio enjoy positive starts
articles.summary: The three teams have collected a respectable 31 points in total after nine games, and all currently sit above the relegation zone.
articles.body:
It was only a few weeks ago that it seemed life in the Premier League might prove a step too far for newly promoted Coventry City .

After storming to the Championship title last season to secure their return to the top flight for the first time since 2001, Frank Lampard's side were given little time to settle into their new surroundings when the campaign began in August.

By the end of their first month back in the Premier League, Coventry were rooted to the bottom of the table, having lost all four of their matches by a combined score of 10-0.

The final defeat of that brutal introduction - a 5-0 hammering at the hands of high-flying Brighton - was enough to convince even the most optimistic supporters that a return to the Championship could be on the cards.

But since that humbling defeat on the south coast almost six weeks ago, Lampard's side have breathed new life into their campaign, winning three of their next five matches.

After back-to-back victories over Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United in September, Saturday's 3-1 win over Sunderland lifted the Sky Blues to 15th in the table.

Coventry are not the only newly promoted side to have impressed, with former Championship rivals Ipswich Town and Hull City also making encouraging starts.

The three teams have collected a combined 31 points after nine games, the 13th-highest tally by promoted sides at this stage in Premier League history.

Hull and Ipswich account for 22 of those points, with Sergej Jakirovic and Gary O'Neil's sides both sitting on 11.

Coventry are slightly behind their promoted peers, but the Sky Blues' three victories have still earned them a respectable nine points.

And there is further encouragement for the newcomers - since the 2010-11 season, all 18 promoted teams who have collected at least 11 points from their opening nine games have avoided relegation.

When reflecting on Coventry 's summer spending spree, it is clear they were under no illusion of what it takes to compete in the Premier League.

The Sky Blues constructed major surgery on their playing squad by shelling out more than £140m on 12 permanent signings.

That splurge included the arrivals of Caleb Yirenkyi for a club-record fee, Carl Rushworth from Brighton , and Sidiki Cherif from Fenerbahce.

Lampard also added Premier League experience in the form of Loum Tchaouna from Burnley and Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest .

After a summer of such upheaval in the West Midlands, it is no surprise it took Lampard a few weeks - five to be exact - to find his winning touch.

Hindsight has also been kind to Coventry . The fact three of their first four Premier League matches were against the current top three - Arsenal , Manchester City and Brighton - was clearly far from the ideal introduction.

After Saturday's 3-1 win over Sunderland , midfielder Jack Rudoni insisted his side still "believed" in their quality after a bruising start to the campaign.

"We always had that belief," Rudoni told BBC Sport. "We have a really good squad here, where the morale is good and we get behind each other, which is what we will continue to do all season.

"We know it's not going to be an easy ride, there's going to be ups and downs - but hopefully more ups than downs. Starting today with another three points, so we can build on that now."

'Our lads have some character and we just need to keep it up'

When Ipswich Town secured their return to the Premier League in May, few expected much from the Tractor Boys.

Their promotion to the top flight in 2024, ending a 22-year absence, exposed just how ill-equipped they were to compete at that level.

By the end of the 2024-25 season, Ipswich finished 19th, recording just four wins from 38 Premier League games.

But having secured an immediate return to the top flight, and after significant investment in the squad over the summer, the Tractor Boys look set to put up more of a fight this time around.

The Championship runners-up's summer business was headlined by the return of Julio Enciso, who spent part of the 2024-25 campaign on loan at Portman Road.

The Paraguay international has been instrumental in Ipswich 's rise this season, assisting their opening goal against Sunderland before setting up another against Manchester United at Old Trafford the following week.

More recently, the 22-year-old has scored in consecutive matches against Nottingham Forest and Hull City , helping his side secure vital points against two teams who could be fighting for Premier League survival come the end of the season.

After Saturday's 2-2 draw with Hull , O'Neil praised his side's "character" after they fought from behind for the second Premier League match in a row.

"It's tough to be in control and find yourselves 2-1 down with the place bouncing," O'Neil told BBC Match of the Day.

"Our lads have some character and we just need to keep it up. Hull are a very good side and I'm really pleased with how we did against them."

Are Hull under pressure despite dream start?

The Premier League season had barely begun when Hull City made waves.

In their first match in the top flight since being relegated in 2017, the Tigers stunned Manchester United with a 2-0 victory on the opening weekend.

Although much of the attention centred on what the result meant for United manager Michael Carrick, Hull were quickly emerging as one of the season's feel-good stories.

Having earned promotion to the Premier League through the Championship play-offs, Jakirovic's side were flying the flag for the promoted clubs in the early weeks of the campaign.

After following up their opening-day triumph with a 1-0 win at Coventry , Hull earned respectable draws against Aston Villa and Chelsea .

But since suffering their first defeat of the season, the Tigers have collected just three points from their four matches since.

And with Arsenal and Brighton up next, the Tigers will know their impressive start could count for little if they fail to add to their points tally soon.

But the Premier League is a marathon, not a sprint - and all three promoted clubs will have belief that they can build on their encouraging starts.

articles.title: Barca hammer Alaves to retain Liga top spot
articles.summary: Raphinha and Lamine Yamal each struck twice as Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damagi...
articles.body:
Raphinha and Lamine Yamal each struck twice as Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats.

Earlier Atletico Madrid, second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved back two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou.

Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend's La Liga home Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick's side found their groove once more.

Raphinha netted twice in the first half, either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval.

Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca's sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves.

"It was a hard week for us, there was no better place than Camp Nou in front of our fans (to bounce back)," Lopez told Movistar.

"They make the difference, Lamine and Raphinha, with them we will achieve big things."

There was a minute's silence at the start of each of the day's matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week.

Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions.

Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga's top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form after Lopez teed him up.

Lopez doubled Barcelona's lead himself in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, he smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it.

Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca's lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal.

Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera.

Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time.

Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up.

Yamal got Barca's fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal.

Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca's sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on.

"For me it was a great game from (Yamal) and it's great to see the level our attacking players are at, Fermin, Raphinha," Flick told reporters.

"This is what I want to see after our two defeats, we reacted in the right way."

Barcelona host Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday and travel to face Atletico next Sunday in a table-topping La Liga clash.

Alaves have now gone seven matches without a win, but are 10th.

"We have to turn the page quickly," said midfielder Ander Guevara. "We don't need to sound the alarms, we know we're on a bad run, but we're a mature and humble team."

Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone's Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante.

Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions.

"I'm very happy with the team's work," Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar.

"We're very far from the end of the season... we'll keep going game by game."

Alex Baena, the visitors' main creative outlet, set up both goals as Simeone recorded his 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club's record set by Luis Aragones.

"I don't feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years," said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011.

On Sunday, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, third, visit Racing Santander among other fixtures.

articles.title: After dueling late 60-yard field goals, No. 4 Indiana escapes Minnesota's upset bid in OT
articles.summary: Just seconds after Minnesota kicked a 60-yard field goal to go ahead, Indiana responded with one of its own.
articles.body:
On a nightmarish special teams day, Indiana got an incredible kick to avoid a second loss of the season.

Seconds after Minnesota kicker Luke Drzewiecki hit a go-ahead 60-yard field goal to put the Gophers up 16-13, Paddy McAteer drained a kick of the same length as time expired in the fourth quarter to get the game to overtime.

From there, Charlie Becker caught a 25-yard pass from Grant Wilson on the first play of the extra period and the Indiana defense prevented Minnesota from getting into the end zone in the Hoosiers' 23-16 win.

Minnesota got inside the Indiana 5-yard line on its overtime possession, but Drake Lindsey was sacked on fourth down after he scrambled for no gain on third down.

The Gophers entered the game as 20.5-point underdogs and the win is Indiana's 29th consecutive against an unranked opponent.

"This is entertainment, so we thought we'd put some entertainment value into this game," Indiana coach Curt Cignetti deadpanned after the game.

Before McAteer's kick, Indiana had missed two field goals, had another gone awry because of a bad snap and shanked a punt. It was a horrific day for the Hoosiers' special teams unit and looked sure to cost them the game after Drzewiecki buried his kick.

However, McAteer stepped up to drain his. Nico Radicic is Indiana's primary kicker — and had missed the two attempts earlier in the game — but McAteer was called on to smash a 60-yarder down the middle with room to spare.

Indiana was fortunate simply to have a chance for McAteer to attempt the kick. After Indiana stopped Minnesota on third down, the Hoosiers had two timeouts remaining. Cignetti didn't use one of those two timeouts, which allowed Minnesota to stop the clock with 24 seconds remaining before attempting the kick.

The special teams mistakes were even more significant because of the way Indiana's offense struggled for much of the game. QB Josh Hoover has appeared to be dealing with an injury sustained in the second half of the Hoosiers' loss to Ohio State. And he took another big hit late in the second half, Cignetti made a QB change.

Grant Wilson opened the second half under center for Indiana, though the Hoosiers immediately punted on that drive. Wilson finished the game 9-of-17 for 156 yards and the TD to Becker after Indiana was initially hesitant to let him throw the ball. Six of Indiana's first seven plays when he entered the game were runs.

Hoover, meanwhile, was 8-of-19 passing for 119 yards and a TD and an interception. A week ago against Michigan, Hoover was just 8-of-18 for 81 yards and a pick in the 13-6 overtime win.
